```gd
	var _alive : WeakRef = weakref(self)
	var _http_ref : WeakRef = weakref(http)
	http.request_completed.connect(ApiConfig.check_clock_skew)
	http.request_completed.connect(func(result, code, _h, body):
		var h = _http_ref.get_ref()
		if h == null or _alive.get_ref() == null: return
		h.queue_free()
		if not cb.is_valid(): return
		if result == HTTPRequest.RESULT_SUCCESS and code == 200:
			var j := JSON.new()
			if j.parse(body.get_string_from_utf8()) == OK:
				var d : Dictionary = j.get_data()
				cb.call(_as_array(d.get("rooms", [])), int(d.get("total", 0)))
				return
		cb.call([], 0)
	)
	http.request(ApiConfig.sign_url(BACKEND_URL + "/backend/vsroom/mine?limit=%d&offset=%d" % [_MINE_PAGE_SIZE, offset]), _headers())


func _fetch_room(room_id: String, cb: Callable) -> void:
	var http := HTTPRequest.new()
	http.timeout = 8.0
	add_child(http)
	# Weakref captures — see _fetch_open. A ?vs= deeplink opens this room right as
	# the list view is torn down, which used to error "Lambda capture was freed".
	var _alive : WeakRef = weakref(self)
	var _http_ref : WeakRef = weakref(http)
	http.request_completed.connect(ApiConfig.check_clock_skew)
	http.request_completed.connect(func(result, code, _h, body):
		var h = _http_ref.get_ref()
		if h == null or _alive.get_ref() == null: return
		h.queue_free()
		if not cb.is_valid(): return
		if result == HTTPRequest.RESULT_SUCCESS and code == 200:
			var j := JSON.new()
			if j.parse(body.get_string_from_utf8()) == OK:
				var d : Dictionary = j.get_data()
				var room : Dictionary = d.get("room", {})
				# join/create responses nest pay_to/pay_memo alongside room —
				# flatten them onto the room dict for _do_pay() to read.
				if d.has("pay_to"):     room["pay_to"]     = d["pay_to"]
				if d.has("pay_memo"):   room["pay_memo"]   = d["pay_memo"]
				if d.has("invite_url"): room["invite_url"] = d["invite_url"]
				if d.has("viewer_is_pending_opponent"): room["viewer_is_pending_opponent"] = d["viewer_is_pending_opponent"]
				cb.call(true, room)
				return
		cb.call(false, {})
	)
	http.request(ApiConfig.sign_url(BACKEND_URL + "/backend/vsroom/" + room_id.uri_encode()), _headers())


func _join_room(room_id: String, cb: Callable) -> void:
	var http := HTTPRequest.new()
	http.timeout = 8.0
	add_child(http)
	# BUG FIX: "Lambda capture at index 0 was freed" — VSPanel (self) or this
	# http node can be freed mid-flight (panel closed/queue_free'd, or a
	# window-resize rebuild) before the response lands.
	var _alive : WeakRef = weakref(self)
	http.request_completed.connect(ApiConfig.check_clock_skew)
	http.request_completed.connect(func(result, code, _h, body):
		if not is_instance_valid(http): return
		http.queue_free()
		if _alive.get_ref() == null: return
		if result == HTTPRequest.RESULT_SUCCESS and code == 200:
			var j := JSON.new()
			if j.parse(body.get_string_from_utf8()) == OK:
				var d : Dictionary = j.get_data()
				var room2 : Dictionary = d.get("room", {})
				if d.has("pay_to"):   room2["pay_to"]   = d["pay_to"]
				if d.has("pay_memo"): room2["pay_memo"] = d["pay_memo"]
				if d.has("viewer_is_pending_opponent"): room2["viewer_is_pending_opponent"] = d["viewer_is_pending_opponent"]
				cb.call(true, room2)
				return
		# BUG FIX: used to always call cb.call(false, {}) on failure, discarding
		# the backend's actual error code (e.g. "slot_reserved_by_another" vs.
		# "room_expired") — callers had no way to show a specific message. Parse
		# the error body (writeErr sends {"error": "..."}) and pass it through.
		var _err_msg := ""
		var ej := JSON.new()
		if ej.parse(body.get_string_from_utf8()) == OK:
			var ed = ej.get_data()
			if typeof(ed) == TYPE_DICTIONARY:
				_err_msg = str(ed.get("error", ""))
		cb.call(false, {"err": _err_msg})
	)
	http.request(ApiConfig.sign_url(BACKEND_URL + "/backend/vsroom/" + room_id.uri_encode() + "/join"), _headers(true), HTTPClient.METHOD_POST, "{}")


## Claims this player's SINGLE play attempt on the server BEFORE the round starts
## — the network-safe lock. cb(ok, room, code, err): ok=true only on a real 200
## (round may start with room.seed). On failure ok=false and (code, err) tell the
## caller whether it was "already_played" (409 — show result/waiting) or a
## transport failure (no/!=200 — "check your connection", DON'T start the round).
func _start_play(room_id: String, cb: Callable) -> void:
	var http := HTTPRequest.new()
	http.timeout = 10.0
	add_child(http)
	var _alive : WeakRef = weakref(self)
	http.request_completed.connect(ApiConfig.check_clock_skew)
	http.request_completed.connect(func(result, code, _h, body):
		if not is_instance_valid(http): return
		http.queue_free()
		if _alive.get_ref() == null: return
		if not cb.is_valid(): return
		if result == HTTPRequest.RESULT_SUCCESS and code == 200:
			var j := JSON.new()
			if j.parse(body.get_string_from_utf8()) == OK:
				var d : Dictionary = j.get_data()
				cb.call(true, d.get("room", {}), 200, "")
				return
			cb.call(false, {}, code, "bad_response")
			return
		# Non-200: pull the backend error code ("already_played", etc.) if present.
		var err_reason := ""
		if body != null:
			var j2 := JSON.new()
			if j2.parse(body.get_string_from_utf8()) == OK:
				var d2 = j2.get_data()
				if d2 is Dictionary: err_reason = str(d2.get("error", ""))
		cb.call(false, {}, code, err_reason)
	)
	http.request(ApiConfig.sign_url(BACKEND_URL + "/backend/vsroom/" + room_id.uri_encode() + "/start"), _headers(true), HTTPClient.METHOD_POST, "{}")


func _confirm_payment(room_id: String, tx_hash: String, cb: Callable) -> void:
	var http := HTTPRequest.new()
	http.timeout = 20.0   # RPC lookup server-side can take a moment
	add_child(http)
	# BUG FIX: "Lambda capture at index 0 was freed" — VSPanel (self) or this
	# http node can be freed mid-flight (panel closed/queue_free'd, or a
	# window-resize rebuild) before the response lands.
	var _alive : WeakRef = weakref(self)
	http.request_completed.connect(ApiConfig.check_clock_skew)
	http.request_completed.connect(func(result, code, _h, body):
		if not is_instance_valid(http): return
		http.queue_free()
		if _alive.get_ref() == null: return
		var ok : bool = result == HTTPRequest.RESULT_SUCCESS and code == 200
		var err_reason := ""
		if not ok and body != null:
			var j := JSON.new()
			if j.parse(body.get_string_from_utf8()) == OK:
				var d = j.get_data()
				if typeof(d) == TYPE_DICTIONARY:
					err_reason = str(d.get("error", ""))
		cb.call(ok, err_reason)
	)
	var body_str := JSON.stringify({"tx_hash": tx_hash})
	http.request(ApiConfig.sign_url(BACKEND_URL + "/backend/vsroom/" + room_id.uri_encode() + "/pay"), _headers(true), HTTPClient.METHOD_POST, body_str)


# ── Mutual forfeit ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Lets a player who's matched into a room (opponent already joined) ask to
# bail out. Nothing actually happens until the OTHER side also requests it —
# see RequestVSForfeit in backend/game/vsroom.go — so this is safe to call
# freely: worst case the request just sits there recorded until the other
# side agrees (or the normal 24h expiry/settlement takes over regardless).
func _request_forfeit(room_id: String, cb: Callable) -> void:
	var http := HTTPRequest.new()
	http.timeout = 8.0
	add_child(http)
	# BUG FIX: "Lambda capture at index 0 was freed" — VSPanel (self) or this
	# http node can be freed mid-flight (panel closed/queue_free'd, or a
	# window-resize rebuild) before the response lands.
	var _alive : WeakRef = weakref(self)
	http.request_completed.connect(ApiConfig.check_clock_skew)
	http.request_completed.connect(func(result, code, _h, body):
		if not is_instance_valid(http): return
		http.queue_free()
		if _alive.get_ref() == null: return
		if result == HTTPRequest.RESULT_SUCCESS and code == 200:
			var j := JSON.new()
			if j.parse(body.get_string_from_utf8()) == OK:
				cb.call(true, j.get_data().get("room", {}))
				return
		cb.call(false, {})
	)
	http.request(ApiConfig.sign_url(BACKEND_URL + "/backend/vsroom/" + room_id.uri_encode() + "/forfeit"), _headers(true), HTTPClient.METHOD_POST, "{}")


# ── Watch replay ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Same fetch pattern as LeaderboardPanel._fetch_and_emit_replay — GET the
# session's replay log and hand it off to Main via replay_requested. The
# backend itself enforces the "not until both sides finished" lock (see
# handleReplay in replay_handlers.go), so this button only ever appears once
# that's already true, but a stale/cached room dict could theoretically still
# show it a moment too early — the 403 from the server just fails quietly.
func _fetch_and_emit_replay(session_id_e: String, btn: Button) -> void:
	if not is_instance_valid(btn): return
	btn.disabled = true
	btn.text = "..."
	var http := HTTPRequest.new()
	http.timeout = 8.0
	add_child(http)
	# BUG FIX: "Lambda capture at index 0 was freed" — VSPanel (self) or this
	# http node can be freed mid-flight (panel closed/queue_free'd, or a
	# window-resize rebuild) before the response lands.
	var _alive : WeakRef = weakref(self)
	http.request_completed.connect(ApiConfig.check_clock_skew)
	http.request_completed.connect(func(result, code, _h, body):
		if not is_instance_valid(http): return
		http.queue_free()
		if _alive.get_ref() == null: return
		if not is_instance_valid(btn): return
		btn.disabled = false
		if result != HTTPRequest.RESULT_SUCCESS or code != 200:
			btn.text = "Replay"
			if code == 403:
				_show_toast_err("Replay isn't unlocked yet — both sides need to finish first.")
			else:
				Toast.network_error("vs_replay_fetch code=%d" % code)
			return
		var j := JSON.new()
		if j.parse(body.get_string_from_utf8()) != OK: return
		var d : Dictionary = j.get_data()
		var seed_str : String = str(d.get("seed", "0"))
		var seed     : int    = int(seed_str)
		var log_b64  : String = str(d.get("replay_log", ""))
		var char_idx : int    = int(d.get("char", 0))
		var gyro_active : bool = bool(d.get("gyro_active", false))
		var nickname : String = str(d.get("nickname", ""))
		var player_seed : int = int(str(d.get("player_seed", "0")))
		var address  : String = str(d.get("player_id", ""))
		if log_b64 == "" or seed == 0: return
		var log_bytes := Marshalls.base64_to_raw(log_b64)
		if log_bytes.is_empty(): return
		replay_requested.emit(seed, log_bytes, char_idx, nickname, player_seed, address, gyro_active)
		hide_panel.call_deferred()
		closed.emit.call_deferred()
	)
	http.request(ApiConfig.sign_url(BACKEND_URL + "/backend/replay/" + session_id_e), _headers())


# ── Nimiq avatars ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Same rendering approach as LeaderboardPanel._make_nimiq_avatar (duplicated
# here rather than shared, matching how QuestPanel/StatsPanel are each
# self-contained): draw a deterministic colored fallback immediately, then
# swap in the real Nimiq identicon once it loads on web.
func _make_nimiq_avatar(address: String, size: int) -> TextureRect:
	var tr := TextureRect.new()
	tr.custom_minimum_size = Vector2(size, size)
	tr.expand_mode    = TextureRect.EXPAND_IGNORE_SIZE
	tr.stretch_mode   = TextureRect.STRETCH_KEEP_ASPECT_CENTERED
	tr.texture_filter = Control.TEXTURE_FILTER_LINEAR
	# If we've already loaded the real identicon for this address+size, use it
	# straight away — no fallback flash, no re-load. This is what stops the VS
	# detail's 4s poll re-render from briefly dropping every avatar back to the
	# colored placeholder before the async load swaps the real one back in.
	var real_key := address + "@" + str(size)
	if _nimiq_avatar_cache.has(real_key):
		tr.texture = _nimiq_avatar_cache[real_key]
		return tr
	tr.texture = _make_fallback_avatar(address, size)
	if OS.has_feature("web") and address != "" and address != "null" and address != "undefined":
		_load_nimiq_avatar_async(tr, address, size)
	return tr


func _make_fallback_avatar(address: String, size: int) -> ImageTexture:
	var cache_key := address + "@" + str(size)
	if _avatar_tex_cache.has(cache_key): return _avatar_tex_cache[cache_key]
	const PALETTE := [
		Color(0.13, 0.60, 0.90),
		Color(0.40, 0.78, 0.22),
		Color(0.96, 0.65, 0.14),
		Color(0.82, 0.28, 0.28),
		Color(0.60, 0.35, 0.85),
		Color(0.20, 0.72, 0.65),
		Color(0.95, 0.38, 0.60),
		Color(0.45, 0.55, 0.70),
	]
	var hash_val := 0
	for i in mini(address.length(), 12):
		hash_val = (hash_val * 31 + address.unicode_at(i)) & 0xFFFF
	var bg_col : Color = PALETTE[hash_val % PALETTE.size()]

	var letter := "?"
	for i in address.length():
		var c := address.unicode_at(i)
		if (c >= 65 and c <= 90) or (c >= 48 and c <= 57):
			letter = address[i]
			break

	var img := Image.create(size, size, false, Image.FORMAT_RGBA8)
	var cx := size * 0.5
	var cy := size * 0.5
	var r  := size * 0.5
	for y in size:
		for x in size:
			var dx := x - cx + 0.5
			var dy := y - cy + 0.5
			if dx * dx + dy * dy <= r * r:
				img.set_pixel(x, y, bg_col)

	var ps := maxi(1, size / 10)
	_draw_letter(img, letter, ps, Color.WHITE)

	var tex := ImageTexture.create_from_image(img)
	_avatar_tex_cache[cache_key] = tex
	return tex


func _draw_letter(img: Image, ch: String, ps: int, ink: Color) -> void:
	const GLYPHS := {
		"0": [0b111,0b101,0b101,0b101,0b111], "1": [0b010,0b110,0b010,0b010,0b111],
		"2": [0b111,0b001,0b111,0b100,0b111], "3": [0b111,0b001,0b111,0b001,0b111],
		"4": [0b101,0b101,0b111,0b001,0b001], "5": [0b111,0b100,0b111,0b001,0b111],
		"6": [0b111,0b100,0b111,0b101,0b111], "7": [0b111,0b001,0b001,0b001,0b001],
		"8": [0b111,0b101,0b111,0b101,0b111], "9": [0b111,0b101,0b111,0b001,0b111],
		"A": [0b010,0b101,0b111,0b101,0b101], "B": [0b110,0b101,0b110,0b101,0b110],
		"C": [0b111,0b100,0b100,0b100,0b111], "D": [0b110,0b101,0b101,0b101,0b110],
		"E": [0b111,0b100,0b110,0b100,0b111], "F": [0b111,0b100,0b110,0b100,0b100],
		"G": [0b111,0b100,0b101,0b101,0b111], "H": [0b101,0b101,0b111,0b101,0b101],
		"I": [0b111,0b010,0b010,0b010,0b111], "J": [0b001,0b001,0b001,0b101,0b111],
		"K": [0b101,0b101,0b110,0b101,0b101], "L": [0b100,0b100,0b100,0b100,0b111],
		"M": [0b101,0b111,0b101,0b101,0b101], "N": [0b101,0b111,0b111,0b101,0b101],
		"O": [0b111,0b101,0b101,0b101,0b111], "P": [0b110,0b101,0b110,0b100,0b100],
		"Q": [0b111,0b101,0b101,0b111,0b001], "R": [0b110,0b101,0b110,0b101,0b101],
		"S": [0b111,0b100,0b111,0b001,0b111], "T": [0b111,0b010,0b010,0b010,0b010],
		"U": [0b101,0b101,0b101,0b101,0b111], "V": [0b101,0b101,0b101,0b010,0b010],
		"W": [0b101,0b101,0b101,0b111,0b101], "X": [0b101,0b101,0b010,0b101,0b101],
		"Y": [0b101,0b101,0b010,0b010,0b010], "Z": [0b111,0b001,0b010,0b100,0b111],
		"?": [0b111,0b001,0b011,0b000,0b010],
	}
	var rows : Array = GLYPHS.get(ch, GLYPHS["?"])
	var w := img.get_width()
	var h := img.get_height()
	var gw := 3 * ps
	var gh := 5 * ps
	var sx := (w - gw) / 2
	var sy := (h - gh) / 2
	for row in 5:
		var mask : int = rows[row]
		for bit in 3:
			if mask & (0b100 >> bit):
				for py in ps:
					for px in ps:
						var ix := sx + bit * ps + px
						var iy := sy + row * ps + py
						if ix >= 0 and ix < w and iy >= 0 and iy < h:
							img.set_pixel(ix, iy, ink)


func _load_nimiq_avatar_async(target: Control, address: String, size: int) -> void:
	if not OS.has_feature("web"): return
	var key := "vsavatar_" + address.left(8).validate_node_name()

	for _w in 30:
		var ready = JavaScriptBridge.eval("window._nimiqIconsReady === true", true)
		if ready: break
		await get_tree().create_timer(0.1).timeout
		if not is_instance_valid(target): return

	# SECURITY: JSON.stringify()'d before splicing into JS (see LeaderboardPanel's
	# _load_nimiq_avatar_async for the same fix + rationale).
	var js_addr := JSON.stringify(address)
	var js_key := JSON.stringify(key)
	var js_code := (
		"(function(){"
		+ "if(!window._nimiqPending) window._nimiqPending = {};"
		+ "window._nimiqPending[" + js_key + "] = null;"
		+ "if(typeof window.getNimiqAvatar !== 'function'){"
		+ "  window._nimiqPending[" + js_key + "] = ''; return;"
		+ "}"
		+ "window.getNimiqAvatar(" + js_addr + ")"
		+ "  .then(function(svgData){"
		+ "    if(!svgData){ window._nimiqPending[" + js_key + "] = ''; return; }"
		+ "    var img = new Image();"
		+ "    img.onload = function(){"
		+ "      try {"
		+ "        var c = document.createElement('canvas');"
		+ "        c.width = " + str(size) + "; c.height = " + str(size) + ";"
		+ "        c.getContext('2d').drawImage(img, 0, 0, " + str(size) + ", " + str(size) + ");"
		+ "        window._nimiqPending[" + js_key + "] = c.toDataURL('image/png');"
		+ "      } catch(e){ window._nimiqPending[" + js_key + "] = ''; }"
		+ "    };"
		+ "    img.onerror = function(){ window._nimiqPending[" + js_key + "] = ''; };"
		+ "    img.src = svgData;"
		+ "  })"
		+ "  .catch(function(e){ window._nimiqPending[" + js_key + "] = ''; });"
		+ "})();"
	)
	JavaScriptBridge.eval(js_code, true)
	for _i in 50:
		await get_tree().create_timer(0.1).timeout
		if not is_instance_valid(target): return
		var raw = JavaScriptBridge.eval("window._nimiqPending[%s]" % js_key, true)
		if raw == null: continue
		var result := str(raw)
		if result == "" or result == "null" or result == "undefined":
			return
		var tex := _png_base64_to_tex(result)
		if tex != null:
			# Cache the real identicon so future re-renders (the 4s poll) reuse it
			# instantly instead of flashing the fallback and re-loading.
			_nimiq_avatar_cache[address + "@" + str(size)] = tex
			if is_instance_valid(target):
				(target as TextureRect).texture = tex
		return


func _png_base64_to_tex(data_url: String) -> ImageTexture:
	if DisplayServer.get_name() == "headless": return null
	if not data_url.begins_with("data:image/png;base64,"): return null
	var b64   := data_url.substr(len("data:image/png;base64,")).strip_edges()
	var bytes := Marshalls.base64_to_raw(b64)
	if bytes.is_empty(): return null
	var img := Image.new()
	if img.load_png_from_buffer(bytes) != OK: return null
	return ImageTexture.create_from_image(img)

```

`game/template/_headers`:

```
# _headers — Cloudflare Pages custom headers
#
# Previously had a Content-Encoding: br rule for /index.wasm — that's
# gone now that build.py splits large wasm files into .part1/.part2
# instead of brotli-compressing them (see setup/build.py, section 5
# of the README). Those parts are raw bytes, not brotli, so keeping
# `Content-Encoding: br` here would make browsers try to brotli-decode
# them and fail.
#
# Whatever goes here gets copied into export/ as-is by build.py on every
# run — this file (in game/template/) is the source of truth, don't edit
# the copy inside export/ directly.
#
# ── CROSS-ORIGIN ISOLATION OFF (Nimiq Hub popup fix) ─────────────────────────
# THE actual root cause of the persistent "Invalid Request" / "Connection was
# closed" error on the Nimiq Hub web sign-in popup. The DEPLOYED page (served
# by Cloudflare Pages, NOT the Go backend) was coming back with:
#     cross-origin-opener-policy: same-origin
#     cross-origin-embedder-policy: require-corp
# i.e. a fully cross-origin-ISOLATED page. Those two together sever the
# window.opener link on ANY cross-origin popup (hub.nimiq.com) — so inside the
# popup window.opener is null, Hub's own 1s connect-timeout handler
# (nimiq/hub RpcApi.ts branches on `window.opener === null`) abandons the
# postMessage handshake and shows its "Invalid Request" page, which our RPC
# client then surfaces as "Connection was closed". This was NOT fixable from
# the Go backend's headers: the HTML document is served by Cloudflare Pages,
# whose header layer is controlled by THIS file — the Go COOP/COEP changes
# only ever applied to /backend/* API responses, never to index.html.
#
# Setting both to their non-isolating values here explicitly OVERRIDES the
# stale/default isolation that was being served, restoring the classic
# behavior where a cross-origin popup keeps its opener — exactly what
# popup-based auth (OAuth, Google Sign-In, Nimiq Hub) needs. Safe: this
# single-threaded Godot export never needed SharedArrayBuffer/threads (see
# index.html's Engine features {threads:false} +
# GODOT_CONFIG['ensureCrossOriginIsolationHeaders']=false), so losing
# crossOriginIsolated/SAB costs nothing.
#
# ── CSP (broad/permissive on purpose) ────────────────────────────────────────
# Fixes "loads to 100%, then the page reloads itself" on some mobile
# browsers/webviews: script-src-elem and connect-src were being blocked by the
# host's default CSP (unpkg.com, wasm/pck fetches). Intentionally wide open for
# now — tighten later (swap https:/wss: wildcards for the real backend + CDN
# domains) once confirmed stable.
#
# NOTE (Cloudflare _headers format): all headers for a path must sit directly
# under the path line with NO blank line between them — a blank line ends the
# rule block. Keep COOP/COEP/CSP contiguous below.
/*
  Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy: unsafe-none
  Cross-Origin-Embedder-Policy: unsafe-none
  Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'self' https: wss: blob: data:; script-src 'self' https: blob: data: 'unsafe-inline' 'unsafe-eval' 'wasm-unsafe-eval'; script-src-elem 'self' https: blob: data: 'unsafe-inline'; worker-src 'self' https: blob: data:; connect-src 'self' https: wss: blob: data:; style-src 'self' https: 'unsafe-inline'; img-src 'self' https: blob: data:; font-src 'self' https: data:; media-src 'self' https: blob: data:; manifest-src 'self' https:; frame-src 'self' https:; child-src 'self' https: blob:; object-src 'none'

```

`game/template/index.html`:

```html
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
  <meta charset="utf-8">
  <meta http-equiv="Cache-Control" content="no-cache, no-store, must-revalidate">
  <meta http-equiv="Pragma" content="no-cache">
  <meta http-equiv="Expires" content="0">
  <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1, viewport-fit=cover">
  <!-- PERF/BUG FIX: Nimiq Hub's own popup (hub.nimiq.com) starts a hardcoded
       1-SECOND timeout the instant it loads (see nimiq/hub's RpcApi.start()
       -> RpcServer.init(onClientTimeout), window.setTimeout(...,1000)) —
       if our client's first ping doesn't reach an already-booted Hub SPA
       within that 1s window, Hub gives up and shows its own "Invalid
       Request" error page, which is what produces the "Connection was
       closed" error our RPC client then sees (confirmed by reading Hub's
       and its rpc library's actual source — this is NOT a popup-blocking or
       user-gesture-timing issue, a genuine synchronous click still hits
       this exact race). The Hub SPA has to do real work in that same
       window — bootstrap its Vue app, AND its Keyguard client/iframe
       (keyguard.nimiq.com) — before it can even start listening for our
       ping. DNS/TLS/connection warmup ahead of time (before the popup ever
       opens) is the one part of that budget we can shave down for free —
       every visitor pays this cost on their very first sign-in attempt.
       Safe unconditionally: no user data sent, browser just resolves DNS/
       opens a TLS connection speculatively. -->
  <link rel="preconnect" href="https://hub.nimiq.com" crossorigin>
  <link rel="dns-prefetch" href="https://hub.nimiq.com">
  <link rel="preconnect" href="https://keyguard.nimiq.com" crossorigin>
  <link rel="dns-prefetch" href="https://keyguard.nimiq.com">
  <title>$GODOT_PROJECT_NAME</title>
  <style>
    html, body {
      margin:0; padding:0; width:100%; height:100%; background:#000; overflow:hidden;
      /* Mobile polish — none of this changes layout, only removes native
         browser chrome/gestures that fight a swipe-controlled game:
         - overscroll-behavior:none stops iOS/Android's rubber-band bounce
           and pull-to-refresh from firing when a swipe starts near the top
           or bottom edge (a real risk here — the whole game is swipe-driven,
           and Chrome's pull-to-refresh gesture starts from the exact same
           edge-drag a player uses to move).
         - -webkit-touch-callout:none stops iOS's long-press "callout" menu
           (copy/save-image popup) from interrupting a held touch mid-swipe.
         - -webkit-user-select/user-select:none stops the OS text-selection
           handles from appearing on a long-press anywhere in the canvas.
         - -webkit-tap-highlight-color:transparent removes the default gray
           flash Android/older iOS draws on every tap — with a custom themed
           UI (UITheme.gd) that flash reads as an unstyled/broken tap state
           rather than the game's own press feedback. */
      overscroll-behavior:none;
      -webkit-touch-callout:none;
      -webkit-user-select:none; user-select:none;
      -webkit-tap-highlight-color:transparent;
    }
    /* ── SAFE AREA (notch / Dynamic Island / home-indicator) ────────────────
       viewport-fit=cover above tells the browser to let the page extend
       full-bleed under the notch/home-indicator instead of auto-letterboxing
       — without this, the actual play surface (canvas) would draw its own
       UI edge-to-edge and iPhone's notch/Dynamic Island or the home-indicator
       bar could sit right on top of real, tappable content (bottom nav bar,
       PLAY button, top HUD). Fix: inset the canvas AND the loading/splash
       overlay by env(safe-area-inset-*) so Godot's own viewport only ever
       spans the actual safe rectangle — nothing GDScript-side needs to know
       about this, every existing anchor/margin in the game continues to be
       relative to "the whole screen" because that's still what Godot sees.
       env(..., 0px) fallback makes this a no-op on any browser that doesn't
       support the safe-area env() variables at all (plain desktop, older
       Android) — html/body's #000 background fills the resulting margin on
       devices that DO have a notch/home-indicator, same color as the splash
       screen so it reads as intentional letterboxing, not a layout bug. */
    #canvas {
      /* BUG FIX: this used to be top/bottom/left/right all set + width:auto/
         height:auto. That looked right on paper (a position:fixed box with
         all four offsets pinned, "auto" filling the gap) but <canvas> is a
         REPLACED element (like <img>/<video>) — per the CSS spec, a
         replaced element's 'auto' width/height in this configuration
         resolves to its INTRINSIC size (canvas defaults to 300x150 CSS px
         with no width/height attribute) instead of stretching to fill the
         left/right or top/bottom gap the way a plain <div> would. That's
         exactly "small canvas stuck in the corner, doesn't fill the
         screen" — the report this fixes. Explicit calc() width/height
         removes the ambiguity entirely: no reliance on replaced-element
         auto-sizing behavior at all, just an exact number every browser
         computes the same way. top/left position it, width/height size it,
         'right'/'bottom' aren't needed (and would over-constrain the box
         if combined with an explicit width/height anyway).

         PERMANENT FIX (bottom nav bar — Quests/Stats/Leaderboard/VS —
         getting covered by the phone's OS nav bar on some devices):
         env(safe-area-inset-bottom) ONLY reports hardware safe areas
         (notch, Dynamic Island, iPhone home-indicator). It does NOT
         report Android's on-screen gesture/3-button nav bar at all —
         there is no CSS env() variable for that. On top of that, a
         plain percentage/vh height on a position:fixed full-screen box
         resolves against the browser's "large viewport" (address bar
         hidden) by default on Chrome/Safari's dynamic-toolbar model, so
         on some phones #canvas was measured taller than what's actually
         visible on screen — GDScript's own bottom bar (positioned from
         that same inflated height) ended up drawn partly behind the OS
         nav bar / collapsed toolbar strip, exactly the "some devices"
         symptom reported.

         Fix: --app-height is written by JS below from
         window.visualViewport.height, which is the one number that
         already excludes BOTH the Android nav bar AND a shown/hidden
         mobile toolbar on every browser that matters here (near-
         universal support). env(safe-area-inset-*) is still subtracted
         on top of that for the iOS notch/home-indicator case, which
         visualViewport does NOT exclude on its own — the two fixes are
         complementary, not redundant, and never double-count on either
         platform. `100dvh` is the fallback for the split second before
         the JS below runs (or in the unlikely case it can't run at
         all); plain `100%` one line above is the last-resort fallback
         for engines with neither. */
      position:fixed;
      top:    env(safe-area-inset-top, 0px);
      left:   env(safe-area-inset-left, 0px);
      width:  calc(100% - env(safe-area-inset-left, 0px) - env(safe-area-inset-right, 0px));
      height: calc(100% - env(safe-area-inset-top, 0px) - env(safe-area-inset-bottom, 0px));
      height: calc(100dvh - env(safe-area-inset-top, 0px) - env(safe-area-inset-bottom, 0px));
      height: calc(var(--app-height, 100dvh) - env(safe-area-inset-top, 0px) - env(safe-area-inset-bottom, 0px));
      outline:none; touch-action:none; image-rendering:pixelated;
    }
    #status, #status-splash, #status-progress { position:fixed; }
    #status {
      top:    env(safe-area-inset-top, 0px);
      left:   env(safe-area-inset-left, 0px);
      width:  calc(100% - env(safe-area-inset-left, 0px) - env(safe-area-inset-right, 0px));
      height: calc(100% - env(safe-area-inset-top, 0px) - env(safe-area-inset-bottom, 0px));
      height: calc(100dvh - env(safe-area-inset-top, 0px) - env(safe-area-inset-bottom, 0px));
      height: calc(var(--app-height, 100dvh) - env(safe-area-inset-top, 0px) - env(safe-area-inset-bottom, 0px));
    }
    #status {
      background-color: $GODOT_SPLASH_COLOR;
      display:flex; flex-direction:column; justify-content:center; align-items:center;
      visibility:hidden;
    }
    /* #status-splash (the splash <img>) needs its own explicit inset:0 —
       it's position:fixed (see the shared selector above) with NO offsets
       of its own, this used to be full-viewport (top:0/left:0/right:0/
       bottom:0) matching the original pre-safe-area-fix code; that's what
       lets its own max-width/max-height:100% + margin:auto below actually
       center it (position:fixed/absolute + all-sides-0 + margin:auto on a
       sized box is a real, classic centering technique — but it only works
       if all four offsets are actually 0, not left unset/auto). Kept
       viewport-relative (not safe-area-inset-relative like #status/#canvas
       above) — same as it always was; the splash is shown for such a short
       window before the engine takes over that this was never worth
       revisiting on its own. */
    #status-splash { top:0; left:0; right:0; bottom:0; }

    /* NOTE: a desktop "letterbox" variant (capping #canvas to the portrait
       aspect ratio + centering it, black bars either side) was tried here
       and reverted on request — the game fills the whole browser window on
       desktop now, same as before, full-bleed. The portrait-only UI (e.g.
       the onboarding overlay's anchor_left=0.08/anchor_right=0.92) can still
       look stretched/wide on a very wide desktop window as a result — that
       tradeoff was chosen deliberately over black bars, not missed. */
    #status-splash { max-height:100%; max-width:100%; margin:auto; }
    #status-splash.show-image--false { display:none; }
    #status-splash.fullsize--true { height:100%; width:100%; object-fit:contain; }
    #status-splash.use-filter--false { image-rendering:pixelated; }
    #status-progress, #status-notice { display:none; }
    #status-progress { bottom:10%; width:50%; margin:0 auto; }
    #status-notice {
      background-color:#5b3943; border-radius:0.5rem; border:1px solid #9b3943;
      color:#e0e0e0; font-family:'Noto Sans','Droid Sans',Arial,sans-serif;
      line-height:1.3; margin:0 2rem; overflow:hidden; padding:1rem; text-align:center; z-index:1;
    }

    /* ── PORTRAIT LOCK ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
       Game is portrait-only. The Screen Orientation API (screen.orientation.
       lock) only works inside an installed/fullscreen PWA on the browsers
       that support it at all (mostly Android Chrome) — plain mobile Safari
       tabs can't be force-locked via JS. So instead of relying on JS lock
       (which silently fails on iOS and leaves the canvas resizing/rotating
       with all the side effects that caused — toasts, panels, anchors going
       stale), this uses a pure-CSS media query: whenever the viewport is
       wider than it is tall on a touch device, hide the game canvas entirely
       and show a "rotate your phone" blocker instead. The canvas never sees
       a landscape size at all, so none of the GDScript resize/orientation
       code ever runs in landscape — nothing to go stale. */
    #rotate-lock {
      display:none;
      position:fixed; inset:0; z-index:9999;
      background:#000;
      color:#e8d9c0;
      flex-direction:column; align-items:center; justify-content:center;
      font-family:'Noto Sans','Droid Sans',Arial,sans-serif;
      text-align:center; padding:0 2rem;
    }
    #rotate-lock .icon { font-size:3rem; margin-bottom:1rem; }
    /* pointer:coarse + hover:none = an actual touchscreen (phone/tablet),
       not a desktop browser window that just happens to be wide — device-
       width breakpoints are unreliable for this, pointer/hover capability
       is the correct modern way to target "real mobile device" specifically.
       BUG FIX (black screen after rotating back to portrait): this used to
       also do `#canvas, #status { display:none !important; }` here. On
       several mobile browsers (notably iOS Safari) setting a canvas that
       has a live WebGL context to display:none frees the GPU context
       outright, and Godot's HTML5/WASM export has no code path to rebuild
       its renderer from a 'webglcontextrestored' event — so rotating back
       to portrait brought the canvas back on screen with a dead renderer
       behind it: permanent black screen, no way to recover except a full
       page reload.
       #rotate-lock already fully covers the screen (position:fixed;
       inset:0; solid #000 background; z-index:9999 above the canvas), so
       it was already 100% hiding the canvas visually WITHOUT any help from
       display:none — the canvas being technically still in the render tree
       underneath was never visible to the player. So the only thing
       display:none was actually still doing was (a) risking exactly the
       context-loss bug above, and (b) letting touches fall through to a
       canvas the player can't see. Fix: drop display:none entirely (keeps
       the WebGL context alive, so rotating back is instant and always
       shows a live game, never a black screen) and replace its only
       useful side effect — blocking stray touches on the hidden canvas —
       with pointer-events:none, which has no effect on the GPU context at
       all. GDScript's own resize handler (_on_viewport_resized in Main.gd)
       already debounces/coalesces rapid resize events and safely no-ops
       its landscape-lock branch (_check_landscape() is intentionally a
       no-op now), so letting it see the brief landscape size while the
       overlay is up is safe. */
    @media (orientation: landscape) and (pointer: coarse) and (hover: none) {
      #rotate-lock { display:flex; }
      #canvas, #status { pointer-events:none; }
    }
  </style>
  <script>
    // ── PERMANENT FIX: real visible height for #canvas/#status ─────────────
    // See the long comment on #canvas above for the full "why" — short
    // version: env(safe-area-inset-bottom) doesn't know about Android's
    // on-screen nav bar, and plain %/vh sizing can be measured against a
    // "toolbar hidden" viewport that's taller than what's actually on
    // screen. window.visualViewport.height is the one value that reliably
    // excludes both, on every browser this game targets, so we mirror it
    // into a CSS var and let #canvas/#status consume it (see height rules
    // above). Runs synchronously here (before body/canvas exist) so the
    // var is already correct for the very first layout/paint — no flash
    // of a wrong size — and again on every event that can change the
    // visible area afterwards.
    (function () {
      // BUG FIX #3 (bottom bar still stuck on some Android WebViews):
      // Real-world logs showed sessions where visualViewport.height (and
      // even window.innerHeight) read as literally 0 on the very first
      // call — before the WebView had actually laid out the page — and
      // then NEVER got corrected, because that first call was the only
      // one that ran: no 'resize'/'scroll' event ever fired afterward on
      // that WebView, so --app-height stayed unset and #canvas silently
      // fell back to plain `100dvh`, which does NOT know about Android's
      // on-screen nav bar. All affected sessions in the logs carried a
      // "; wv)" token in the UA — Android's embedded WebView, not a
      // normal Chrome tab — which is known to fire viewport/resize
      // events less reliably than a real browser.
      //
      // Fix has three parts:
      //   1) Reject h<=0 readings (as before) but ALSO retry shortly
      //      after via rAF + timeouts, instead of only trying once —
      //      covers the "layout wasn't ready yet" case.
      //   2) Add a ResizeObserver on <html> as an extra signal source.
      //      WebViews that don't fire visualViewport resize/scroll
      //      reliably still generally fire ResizeObserver correctly,
      //      since it's driven by actual layout, not a separate event
      //      pipeline.
      //   3) A slow poll (every 1s for the first 10s, then stop) as a
      //      last-resort safety net for the rare WebView where neither
      //      of the above fires at all after the initial bad reading.
      var _lastAppHeight = 0;
      function setAppHeight() {
        var vv = window.visualViewport;
        var h = vv ? vv.height : window.innerHeight;
        if (h > 0 && h !== _lastAppHeight) {
          _lastAppHeight = h;
          document.documentElement.style.setProperty('--app-height', h + 'px');
        }
        // BUG FIX (touches near the bottom bar land on the wrong Y on some
        // phones): #canvas's CSS box height already tracks --app-height
        // above, but Godot maps touch coordinates using the ratio between
        // that CSS box and the canvas's actual backing-store resolution
        // (canvas.width/height in device pixels). That backing store used
        // to be set ONCE, at engine-init time, by a separate DPR-capping
        // snippet (see initGodotGame below) that took a single
        // getBoundingClientRect() snapshot and never re-read it. Whenever
        // the nav bar height settles after that snapshot, or appears mid-
        // session (Android's swipe-to-show gesture bar), the CSS box
        // resizes via --app-height but the backing store doesn't — so the
        // two go out of sync and touches map to the wrong internal Y,
        // right in the strip where the bottom bar (Quests/Stats/
        // Leaderboard/VS) lives. Fix: re-sync the backing store from
        // every one of THIS function's callers too, instead of only once.
        // syncCanvasBackingStore is defined later (needs #canvas to
        // exist); guard for the calls that happen before that.
        if (window._syncCanvasBackingStore) window._syncCanvasBackingStore();
        return h;
      }

      setAppHeight();
      // Retry quickly in case the very first call landed before the
      // WebView had a real layout size yet (the h<=0 case from the logs).
      requestAnimationFrame(setAppHeight);
      setTimeout(setAppHeight, 50);
      setTimeout(setAppHeight, 250);

      if (window.visualViewport) {
        // 'resize' covers nav bar show/hide, toolbar show/hide, keyboard
        // open/close; 'scroll' covers iOS Safari's toolbar-collapse-on-
        // scroll changing the visual viewport without a resize event.
        window.visualViewport.addEventListener('resize', setAppHeight);
        window.visualViewport.addEventListener('scroll', setAppHeight);
      }
      // Fallback path for the rare engine without visualViewport at all,
      // and an extra signal alongside it for WebViews that under-fire
      // visualViewport's own events.
      window.addEventListener('resize', setAppHeight);
      window.addEventListener('orientationchange', function () {
        // orientationchange can fire a tick before the viewport actually
        // settles at its new size on some Android builds; re-check shortly
        // after in addition to the immediate call.
        setAppHeight();
        setTimeout(setAppHeight, 300);
      });
      document.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', setAppHeight);

      // Extra signal source: fires on real layout changes even on
      // WebViews that don't dispatch visualViewport resize/scroll
      // reliably. Cheap and safe to leave running for the page's life.
      if (window.ResizeObserver) {
        try {
          new ResizeObserver(function () { setAppHeight(); })
            .observe(document.documentElement);
        } catch (e) { /* never let a diagnostic helper break the page */ }
      }

      // Last-resort safety net: short polling window to catch the case
      // where a WebView fires none of the above after an initial h<=0
      // reading. Stops itself after 10s so it's not a perpetual timer.
      var _pollCount = 0;
      var _pollTimer = setInterval(function () {
        _pollCount++;
        setAppHeight();
        if (_pollCount >= 10) clearInterval(_pollTimer);
      }, 1000);
    })();
  </script>

  <!-- ── DEV MODE ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

  <!-- ── NIMIQ SDK ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── -->
  <script data-cfasync="false" type="module">
    window._nimiqReady    = undefined;
    window._nimiqAddress  = '';
    window._nimiqLabel    = '';
    window._nimiqAvatar   = '';
    window._nimiqDeviceId = '';
    window._nimiqData     = null;

    // BUG FIX (web sign-in sometimes routes to the Nimiq-Pay-only flow even
    // in a plain browser, silently skipping the Hub API popup entirely):
    // Main.gd's Play/Connect-Wallet handlers used to decide mini-app-SDK vs
    // Hub-API routing by reading ONLY window._nimiqProviderMissing — which
    // _initNimiq() below never sets until its OWN async handshake actually
    // finishes rejecting: a fixed 3.5s startup delay, PLUS sdk.init()'s own
    // internal 10s timeout, PLUS an unpkg module fetch — worst case ~15s+
    // before it's ever set. A player who taps Play quickly (the completely
    // normal case) hits that check while it's still `undefined`, which read
    // as `false` — the code then treated "not yet confirmed missing" as
    // "assume still might be Nimiq Pay", took the mini-app-SDK detour
    // (which can never succeed outside Nimiq Pay), burned its own several
    // seconds of internal timeouts, and only fell through to a guest/no-
    // wallet start — the Hub API path was never even reached. window.nimiq
    // and window._nimiqReady are also both still unset at that same early
    // moment for the exact same reason, so none of the three ever help fast
    // enough on their own.
    //
    // window._nimiqInsidePayNow() fixes this by checking window.nimiqPay
    // too — the flag Nimiq Pay's own WebView host injects directly, IN
    // ADDITION to (not instead of) window.nimiq/_nimiqReady — so a genuine
    // Nimiq Pay session is very unlikely to still show false the instant a
    // real user gesture (a Play tap) can happen at all. Exposed as its own
    // always-defined global (NOT nested inside the dismissible Nimiq-Pay-
    // banner IIFE further below, which early-returns and skips its own
    // internal copy of this same check entirely once the banner has been
    // dismissed once this session) so GDScript can call it synchronously,
    // with zero waiting, at the exact moment of any Play/Connect tap.
    window._nimiqInsidePayNow = function() {
      return !!(window.nimiqPay || window.nimiq || window._nimiqReady);
    };

    async function _initNimiq() {
      try {
        // Pinned (was @latest) — this package is still 0.x, so @latest could
        // silently pull a behavior-breaking update (e.g. changing how
        // listAccounts()/connect() persist across sessions, which is exactly
        // the kind of change that would look like "keeps asking to
        // reconnect/resign for no reason" with zero corresponding change on
        // our side or in the backend logs). Bump this deliberately, on
        // purpose, after testing — never let it float again.
        const sdk = await import('https://unpkg.com/@nimiq/mini-app-sdk@0.1.0/dist/index.js');
        let nimiq;
        try {
          nimiq = await sdk.init({ timeout: 10000 });
          window.nimiq = nimiq;
        } catch(e) {
          if (window._DEV) console.warn('[Nimiq] Provider not found:', e);
          window._nimiqProviderMissing = true; // definitive: we are NOT inside Nimiq Pay
          return;
        }
        let address = '';
        try {
          const listed = await nimiq.listAccounts();
          if (Array.isArray(listed) && listed.length > 0 && typeof listed[0] === 'string') address = listed[0];
        } catch(e) { if (window._DEV) console.warn('[Nimiq] listAccounts:', e); }
        if (!address) {
          try {
            await nimiq.connect();
            const listed2 = await nimiq.listAccounts();
            if (Array.isArray(listed2) && listed2.length > 0 && typeof listed2[0] === 'string') address = listed2[0];
          } catch(e) { if (window._DEV) console.warn('[Nimiq] connect:', e); }
        }
        window._nimiqAddress = address ? String(address) : '';
        window._nimiqLabel   = address ? String(address).slice(0, 9) : '';
        // REMOVED per request: sdk.requestDeviceIdentifier({reason:'NimJump score
        // ranking'}) used to fire here on every load — this is what triggered
        // Nimiq Pay's native "allow device identifier" permission prompt the
        // first time a player opened the game, citing leaderboard ranking as
        // the reason. Dropped entirely; window._nimiqDeviceId stays '' (see
        // init above), so guests without a connected wallet just don't get a
        // persistent cross-session id — wallet connect is the only path to a
        // saved rank now, no separate permission prompt.
        window._nimiqLanguage = (window.nimiqPay && window.nimiqPay.language)
          || (navigator.language ? navigator.language.split('-')[0] : 'en');
        window._nimiqData = { address: window._nimiqAddress, label: window._nimiqLabel, deviceId: window._nimiqDeviceId, _provider: nimiq };
        try {
          if (window._nimiqAddress && window.getNimiqAvatar)
            window._nimiqAvatar = await window.getNimiqAvatar(window._nimiqAddress) || '';
        } catch(e) { window._nimiqAvatar = ''; }
        window._nimiqReady = true;
      } catch(e) {
        if (window._DEV) console.warn('[Nimiq] SDK load failed:', e);
        window._nimiqProviderMissing = true; // SDK itself failed to load -> definitely not inside Nimiq Pay
      }
    }
    setTimeout(function() {
      if (typeof requestIdleCallback !== 'undefined') requestIdleCallback(_initNimiq, { timeout: 2000 });
      else _initNimiq();
    }, 3500);
  </script>

  <!-- ── NIMIQ HUB API (web browser sign-in) ─────────────────────────────────
       Only relevant OUTSIDE Nimiq Pay: real wallet sign-in for players who
       open the game in a plain browser tab. This is a SEPARATE integration
       from the mini-app SDK above (_initNimiq) — that one only initializes
       inside Nimiq Pay's own host and rejects everywhere else (sets
       window._nimiqProviderMissing), so it can never work standalone. The
       Hub API talks to hub.nimiq.com directly via a popup and works in any
       normal browser.

       BUG FIX ("Invalid Request" from hub.nimiq.com, persisting even after
       the COOP/COEP fixes in main.go): Nimiq's own docs are explicit that
       Hub API methods "must be called synchronously within a user action,
       such as a click" (https://nimiq.github.io/hub/usage#calling-methods).
       This used to be lazy-loaded — _loadHubApi() only started its dynamic
       import() of the CDN module the FIRST time window._nimiqHubSign() was
       actually called, i.e. from inside the Play/Connect tap's own handler.
       A dynamic import() is a real network fetch, not a same-tick
       microtask — by the time it resolved and hubApi.signMessage() (which
       internally does window.open()) finally ran, the click's transient
       user-activation window had already elapsed. The popup could still
       open (window.open() doesn't hard-require activation in every
       browser), but without a genuine synchronous-gesture-linked open,
       hub.nimiq.com's own client-side RPC handshake with our page
       apparently doesn't reliably complete — surfacing as "Invalid
       Request"/timeout on Hub's side. Fix: kick off _loadHubApi() eagerly,
       right away on page load (below), instead of waiting for the first
       sign attempt — a small, harmless module fetch everyone already pays
       for anyway once Godot itself finishes loading. By the time a player
       can realistically tap Play/Connect, window._HubApiCtor is normally
       already resolved, so window._nimiqHubSign() below calls
       hubApi.signMessage() (and therefore window.open()) IMMEDIATELY,
       fully synchronously inside the click handler's own call stack — no
       .then() in between. The old lazy/async path is kept ONLY as a
       fallback for the rare case where the module genuinely hasn't finished
       loading yet by click-time (very slow network) — that fallback can
       still hit the same popup-blocking risk this fix is otherwise
       eliminating, but it's now the rare edge case, not the default path.
       IMPORTANT (unchanged): window._nimiqHubSign() must still only ever be
       called from a real user gesture (a button's pressed handler) — see
       NimiqJS.gd's start_hub_sign() doc comment. -->
  <script data-cfasync="false">
  (function() {
    var DEV = window._DEV;
    var _hubApiPromise = null;

    function _bytesToHex(bytes) {
      var hex = '';
      for (var i = 0; i < bytes.length; i++) {
        var b = bytes[i].toString(16);
        hex += (b.length === 1 ? '0' + b : b);
      }
      return hex;
    }

    // Dynamic import, same pattern as the identicons library above. Version
    // pinned (see the mini-app SDK comment above for why: an unpinned
    // @latest could silently pull a behavior-breaking update with zero
    // corresponding change on our side). Kicked off EAGERLY below (not
    // waiting for the first sign attempt) — see this script block's
    // top-of-file doc comment for why: window.open() needs to fire
    // synchronously inside the click handler, which is only possible if
    // this module is already loaded by the time a real Play/Connect tap
    // happens.
    function _loadHubApi() {
      if (_hubApiPromise) return _hubApiPromise;
      _hubApiPromise = new Promise(function(resolve, reject) {
        window._HubApiCtor = null;
        var s = document.createElement('script');
        s.type = 'module';
        s.textContent = [
          'import HubApi from "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@nimiq/hub-api@v1.2.3/dist/standalone/HubApi.standalone.es.js";',
          'window._HubApiCtor = HubApi;'
        ].join('\n');
        document.head.appendChild(s);
        var waited = 0;
        var poll = setInterval(function() {
          waited += 100;
          if (window._HubApiCtor) {
            clearInterval(poll);
            resolve(window._HubApiCtor);
          } else if (waited >= 15000) {
            clearInterval(poll);
            reject(new Error('hub_api_load_timeout'));
          }
        }, 100);
      });
      return _hubApiPromise;
    }

    var _hubApiInstance = null;
    function _getHubApi(HubApiCtor) {
      if (!_hubApiInstance) {
        // Mainnet endpoint — matches the backend's default NIMIQ_NETWORK=
        // mainnet (see backend/.env.example). Swap to
        // 'https://hub.nimiq-testnet.com' if this deployment ever runs
        // against testnet.
        _hubApiInstance = new HubApiCtor('https://hub.nimiq.com');
      }
      return _hubApiInstance;
    }

    // Called from GDScript (NimiqJS.gd's start_hub_sign()). Writes result to
    // document.body.dataset.nimiqHubSign — same async-callback-via-DOM-dataset
    // pattern used by the mini-app SDK's start_sign() (see NimiqJS.gd),
    // because Emscripten's JavaScriptBridge.eval() can't directly await a
    // JS Promise from GDScript.
    // Result shape: {ok:true, address, publicKey (hex), signature (hex)}
    //            or {ok:false, err}
    // NOTE: unlike the mini-app SDK path, Hub API's signMessage() returns the
    // signer's address directly in the SAME popup interaction — no separate
    // "connect"/"listAccounts" round trip needed first.
    function _finishHubSign(promise) {
      promise.then(function(result) {
        var pubHex = _bytesToHex(result.signerPublicKey);
        var sigHex = _bytesToHex(result.signature);
        document.body.dataset.nimiqHubSign = JSON.stringify({
          ok: true, address: result.signer, publicKey: pubHex, signature: sigHex
        });
        console.log('[HubSign] ok addr=' + result.signer);
      }).catch(function(err) {
        var msg = (err && err.message) ? err.message : String(err);
        console.warn('[HubSign] failed:', err, msg);
        document.body.dataset.nimiqHubSign = JSON.stringify({ ok: false, err: msg });
      });
    }
    // DIAGNOSTIC (deliberately NOT gated behind `if (DEV)` — this is the one
    // thing we actually need to see in a real player's console to tell
    // whether a given build/deploy is even running this fix at all, vs an
    // older cached build, vs the fix running but hub.nimiq.com still
    // rejecting for some other reason). Safe to remove once this is
    // confirmed working across a few real tests.
    console.log('[HubSign] script loaded, build tag=eager-preload-v1');

    window._nimiqHubSign = function(message) {
      document.body.dataset.nimiqHubSign = '';
      // FAST PATH (the normal case — see this file's top-of-block doc
      // comment): the eager preload below has almost certainly already
      // resolved window._HubApiCtor by the time a real Play/Connect tap can
      // happen, so call signMessage() (and therefore window.open())
      // IMMEDIATELY here, with zero .then()/microtask hop, so it runs
      // inside this click handler's own synchronous call stack.
      if (window._HubApiCtor) {
        console.log('[HubSign] FAST PATH — calling signMessage synchronously');
        _finishHubSign(_getHubApi(window._HubApiCtor).signMessage({ appName: 'NimJump', message: message }));
        return;
      }
      // SLOW-NETWORK FALLBACK ONLY: module genuinely isn't ready yet. This
      // still risks the popup-blocking/handshake issue the eager preload
      // exists to avoid, but it's strictly better than never attempting at
      // all, and should be rare in practice.
      console.warn('[HubSign] SLOW PATH — _HubApiCtor not ready yet at click time, falling back to async load (popup may be blocked)');
      _finishHubSign(_loadHubApi().then(function(HubApiCtor) {
        return _getHubApi(HubApiCtor).signMessage({ appName: 'NimJump', message: message });
      }));
    };

    // ── WEB PAYMENT via Hub API checkout ────────────────────────────────────
    // Counterpart to _nimiqHubSign for PAYMENTS (VS room entry fee, cosmetics).
    // Inside Nimiq Pay, NimiqJS.start_payment() uses the mini-app SDK's
    // window.nimiq.sendBasicTransactionWithData(). On a plain web browser there
    // is no window.nimiq provider (that's the "payment failed: no_provider"
    // error), so payments must go through the Hub API's checkout() popup — the
    // same channel web sign-in uses. checkout() opens the Hub popup, the user
    // confirms, Hub broadcasts the NIM transaction to the network, and returns
    // a SignedTransaction whose hash the backend then verifies on-chain
    // (getTransactionByHash — see backend/game/vsroom.go). Result is written to
    // document.body.dataset.nimiqPay in the SAME {ok,tx}/{ok,err} shape the
    // native path uses, so NimiqJS.await_payment() needs no changes.
    // MUST be called synchronously from a real user gesture (the "Pay" button's
    // pressed handler) for the popup not to be blocked — same as _nimiqHubSign.
    function _finishHubCheckout(promise) {
      promise.then(function(result) {
        // Hub's SignedTransaction exposes the on-chain tx hash as .hash; guard
        // across Hub versions with a couple of fallbacks just in case.
        var hash = (result && (result.hash || result.transactionHash
          || (result.raw && result.raw.hash))) || '';
        document.body.dataset.nimiqPay = JSON.stringify({ ok: true, tx: String(hash) });
        console.log('[HubCheckout] ok tx=' + hash);
      }).catch(function(err) {
        var msg = (err && err.message) ? err.message : String(err);
        console.warn('[HubCheckout] failed:', err, msg);
        document.body.dataset.nimiqPay = JSON.stringify({ ok: false, err: msg });
      });
    }
    window._nimiqHubCheckout = function(recipient, valueLuna, extraData) {
      document.body.dataset.nimiqPay = '';
      var req = { appName: 'NimJump', recipient: recipient, value: valueLuna };
      if (extraData) req.extraData = extraData;  // the "vs:<room>:<c|o>" memo tag
      if (window._HubApiCtor) {
        console.log('[HubCheckout] FAST PATH — calling checkout synchronously');
        _finishHubCheckout(_getHubApi(window._HubApiCtor).checkout(req));
        return;
      }
      console.warn('[HubCheckout] SLOW PATH — _HubApiCtor not ready yet at click time, falling back to async load (popup may be blocked)');
      _finishHubCheckout(_loadHubApi().then(function(HubApiCtor) {
        return _getHubApi(HubApiCtor).checkout(req);
      }));
    };

    // Eager preload — see this script block's top-of-file doc comment.
    // Fire-and-forget: any failure here just means _nimiqHubSign() falls
    // back to the slow-network path above when actually needed; nothing
    // else depends on this promise directly.
    console.log('[HubSign] eager preload starting...');
    _loadHubApi().then(function() {
      console.log('[HubSign] eager preload finished OK — _HubApiCtor ready');
    }).catch(function(err) {
      console.warn('[HubSign] eager preload failed (will retry on demand):', err);
    });
  })();
  </script>

  <script data-cfasync="false">

  <!-- ── NATIVE AUDIO ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────── -->
  <script data-cfasync="false">
  (function() {
    var _sounds  = {};
    // BUG FIX: Master default here was 1.0, but Main.gd's fresh-user default
    // is 0.5 (see _volume var). Godot's _apply_audio_settings() overwrites
    // this with the real value on every boot, so in the normal case it never
    // mattered — but keeping the two in sync removes any window (e.g. a sound
    // firing before Godot's WASM finishes booting and calling _gdSetBus) where
    // a fresh user could hear full-volume audio instead of the intended
    // quieter default.
    var _busVol  = { BGM:0.55, SFX_Jump:0.85, SFX_Damage:0.90, Master:0.5 };
    var _busMute = { BGM:false, SFX_Jump:false, SFX_Damage:false, Master:false };
    var _unlocked = false;

    function _effVol(bus) {
      if (_busMute[bus] || _busMute.Master) return 0;
      // BUG FIX: "x || 1" treats a real 0 (slider dragged all the way down —
      // fully muted) as "unset" and silently snaps it back to full volume 1.
      // _busVol always has real defaults seeded above, so there's no actual
      // "unset" case to guard against — use the stored value as-is.
      var b = _busVol[bus];
      var m = _busVol.Master;
      if (typeof b !== 'number' || isNaN(b)) b = 1;
      if (typeof m !== 'number' || isNaN(m)) m = 1;
      return Math.max(0, Math.min(1, b * m));
    }
    function _reg(name, url, bus, loop) {
      var a = new Audio();
      a.src=url; a.preload='auto'; a.loop=!!loop;
      a.addEventListener('error', function(){ if(window._DEV) console.warn('[Audio] load failed: '+name); });
      _sounds[name] = { audio:a, bus:bus };
    }
    // bgm switched from .wav (13.6MB, uncompressed 44.1kHz/16-bit) to .ogg
    // (Vorbis q4, ~1.2MB) — same track, ~11x smaller download on first load.
    // Native <audio> plays OGG Vorbis fine on every browser this game
    // targets (Chrome/Safari/Firefox, desktop+mobile); no fallback needed.
    _reg('bgm',    'assets/audio/bgm.ogg',    'BGM',      true);
    _reg('jump',   'assets/audio/jump.wav',   'SFX_Jump', false);
    _reg('damage', 'assets/audio/damage.wav', 'SFX_Damage', false);

    // BUG FIX ("ses açıktı ama oyun açıldı çalışmadı, ayarlardan aç kapa
    // yapınca geri geldi, nadiren oldu"): bgm_play's `s.audio.play()` call
    // below is `.catch(function(){})` — a silent swallow. The browser's
    // autoplay policy can reject that specific play() attempt (the WASM
    // round-trip from the real DOM gesture to this JS call isn't always
    // still within the browser's "transient activation" window by the time
    // it runs, so the very first bgm_play after boot is the one most at
    // risk) with zero visible error. Main.gd's _start_bgm_if_needed() used
    // to mark BGM as "started" the instant it SENT the play command, with no
    // way to know the attempt actually failed — so a silently-rejected first
    // attempt left music dead for the rest of the session, since nothing
    // ever re-sent bgm_play once that flag was set. Track the real,
    // browser-confirmed playback state here (the 'playing' event only fires
    // once the browser has actually started producing sound; 'pause'/'ended'
    // cover both an explicit stop AND the promise-rejection case, since a
    // rejected play() reverts the element to paused) so GDScript can check
    // "did it ACTUALLY start" instead of just trusting its own outgoing
    // command, and retry if not.
    window._bgmActuallyPlaying = false;
    _sounds.bgm.audio.addEventListener('playing', function(){ window._bgmActuallyPlaying = true; });
    _sounds.bgm.audio.addEventListener('pause',   function(){ window._bgmActuallyPlaying = false; });
    _sounds.bgm.audio.addEventListener('ended',   function(){ window._bgmActuallyPlaying = false; });

    window._gdSound = function(cmd) {
      if (cmd === 'unlock') { _unlocked=true; return; }
      if (!_unlocked) return;
      var s;
      if (cmd === 'bgm_play') {
        s=_sounds.bgm; if(s&&s.audio.paused){ s.audio.volume=_effVol('BGM'); s.audio.play().catch(function(){}); }
      } else if (cmd === 'bgm_stop') {
        s=_sounds.bgm; if(s){s.audio.pause();s.audio.currentTime=0;}
      } else if (cmd === 'jump_play') {
        s=_sounds.jump; if(s){s.audio.currentTime=0;s.audio.volume=_effVol('SFX_Jump');s.audio.play().catch(function(){});}
      } else if (cmd === 'damage_play') {
        s=_sounds.damage; if(s){s.audio.currentTime=0;s.audio.volume=_effVol('SFX_Damage');s.audio.play().catch(function(){});}
      }
    };
    window._gdSetBus = function(bus, vol, muted) {
      _busVol[bus]=parseFloat(vol)||0;
      _busMute[bus]=(muted===true||muted==='true');
      // BUG FIX: this used to only refresh sounds whose OWN bus matches the
      // bus that just changed — but nothing is ever registered with
      // bus==='Master' (sounds are tagged 'BGM'/'SFX_Jump'/'SFX_Damage'), so
      // a Master-only change (the master mute toggle) matched ZERO sounds
      // here and never touched their actual <audio>.volume at all. Master
      // mute state itself was still recorded correctly (_effVol reads it),
      // but any sound that doesn't recompute its volume fresh right before
      // playing (i.e. an already-looping BGM) kept whatever volume it had
      // from before — so toggling mute while BGM was already playing didn't
      // reliably (im)mute it via THIS path (bgm_stop covers the mute-BGM
      // case separately, but this is the general fix). When bus is 'Master',
      // refresh every registered sound's volume, not just an (empty) subset.
      Object.keys(_sounds).forEach(function(n){
        if (bus === 'Master' || _sounds[n].bus === bus) _sounds[n].audio.volume = _effVol(_sounds[n].bus);
      });
    };
    function _unlock(){ _unlocked=true; }
    ['touchstart','mousedown','keydown','click'].forEach(function(ev){
      document.addEventListener(ev,_unlock,{once:true,capture:true,passive:true});
    });
  })();
  </script>

  <!-- ── NIMIQ PAY BANNER ───────────────────────────────────────────────────── -->
  <script data-cfasync="false">
  (function() {
    // Deep-link host resolution mirrors ApiConfig.gd's game_url():
    //   1. ?game_url= query param
    //   2. localStorage 'nj_game_url'
    //   3. this page's own origin (window.location.origin)
    //   4. hardcoded last-resort fallback (only if all else fails)
    function resolveGameHost() {
      try {
        var q = (new URLSearchParams(window.location.search)).get('game_url');
        if (q) return q.replace(/^https?:\/\//, '').replace(/\/$/, '');
      } catch(e) {}
      try {
        var ls = localStorage.getItem('nj_game_url');
        if (ls) return ls.replace(/^https?:\/\//, '').replace(/\/$/, '');
      } catch(e) {}
      if (window.location.origin && window.location.origin !== 'null') {
        return window.location.origin.replace(/^https?:\/\//, '').replace(/\/$/, '');
      }
      return ''; // nothing resolved — deep link will be built without a host
    }
    // BUG FIX: resolveGameHost() above only ever returns the bare host —
    // it strips protocol/trailing-slash on purpose, but callers then used
    // ONLY that host for the deep link, silently dropping the current
    // page's own path+query string (e.g. "?vs=id"). That's exactly the
    // param that identifies the session/referral/auto-payout trigger, so
    // whoever tapped the button while on <host>?vs=id got dropped into
    // Nimiq Pay at the bare host with no ?vs=id at all — no session id,
    // no auto NIM payout.
    // Fix: append the CURRENT page's pathname+search (not just re-derive
    // from ?game_url=, which may not even be present) onto the resolved
    // host, so the deep link reopens the exact same URL+params inside
    // Nimiq Pay. Left unencoded on purpose — matches the existing
    // "url=" + host concatenation style below (Nimiq Pay's own deep-link
    // parser expects the raw url, not a URI-encoded one), and since this
    // is the LAST/only param on the nimiqpay:// scheme, the embedded "?"
    // and "&" from our own query string don't collide with anything.
    function currentPathAndQuery() {
      try { return window.location.pathname + window.location.search; }
      catch(e) { return ''; }
    }
    var _host = resolveGameHost();
    var _target = _host ? (_host + currentPathAndQuery()) : '';
    var DEEP_LINK = _target ? ('nimiqpay://miniapp?url=' + _target) : '';
    try { if (sessionStorage.getItem('nq_banner_dismissed')==='1') return; } catch(e) {}

    // We're already inside Nimiq Pay if either the host injects window.nimiqPay,
    // or our own SDK init (see _initNimiq above) found a wallet provider and set
    // window.nimiq / window._nimiqReady.
    function insideNimiqPay() {
      return !!(window.nimiqPay || window.nimiq || window._nimiqReady);
    }
    // Definitive negative: _initNimiq's sdk.init() rejected ("provider not found")
    // or the SDK failed to load entirely — this is the real "we are NOT in Nimiq
    // Pay" signal, set by the NIMIQ SDK script above. Only fires from here.
    function providerConfirmedMissing() {
      return !!window._nimiqProviderMissing;
    }

    // ── "Get Nimiq Pay" store link + fallback popup ─────────────────────────
    // BUG FIX: the "Open ↗" button just fired the nimiqpay:// custom-scheme
    // deep link and stopped there — if Nimiq Pay isn't actually installed
    // (the common case for someone hitting the game link from a tweet/share/
    // search result), a custom scheme the OS doesn't recognize does NOTHING
    // visible at all: no error, no fallback, button just looks broken. Same
    // gap existed for "Connect Wallet" inside the game (StatsPanel/QuestPanel/
    // LeaderboardPanel) when there's no provider to connect to — it silently
    // no-ops instead of telling the player what to do. Both now go through
    // this one popup: real per-platform store link (iOS App Store / Android
    // Play Store ids below are Nimiq Pay's actual listing, confirmed live),
    // desktop falls back to the informational nimiq.com/nimiq-pay/ page since
    // there's no store link that makes sense there.
    var STORE_URL_IOS     = 'https://apps.apple.com/us/app/nimiq-pay/id6471844738';
    var STORE_URL_ANDROID = 'https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.nimiq.pay';
    var STORE_URL_DESKTOP = 'https://www.nimiq.com/nimiq-pay/';

    function getNimiqStoreUrl() {
      var ua = navigator.userAgent || '';
      var isIOS = /iPad|iPhone|iPod/.test(ua) ||
        (navigator.platform === 'MacIntel' && navigator.maxTouchPoints > 1); // iPadOS 13+ UA quirk
      if (isIOS) return STORE_URL_IOS;
      if (/Android/i.test(ua)) return STORE_URL_ANDROID;
      return STORE_URL_DESKTOP;
    }

    function showInstallPopup() {
      if (document.getElementById('nq-install-popup')) return; // don't stack duplicates
      var overlay = document.createElement('div');
      overlay.id = 'nq-install-popup';
      overlay.style.cssText = 'position:fixed;inset:0;z-index:99999;background:rgba(0,0,0,.6);' +
        'display:flex;align-items:center;justify-content:center;font-family:sans-serif;padding:24px;box-sizing:border-box';
      var card = document.createElement('div');

        'width:100%;text-align:center;box-shadow:0 8px 32px rgba(0,0,0,.5)';
      var title = document.createElement('div');
      title.textContent = 'Get Nimiq Pay';
      title.style.cssText = 'font-size:18px;font-weight:bold;margin-bottom:10px';
      var body = document.createElement('div');
      body.textContent = "Looks like you don't have Nimiq Pay installed yet — install it to connect your wallet and earn 2× the NIM rewards. Web play pays only half.";
      body.style.cssText = 'font-size:14px;line-height:1.4;color:#cfd0e0;margin-bottom:18px';
      var getBtn = document.createElement('button');
      getBtn.textContent = 'Get Nimiq Pay ↗';
      getBtn.style.cssText = 'background:#f6b221;color:#1a1a2e;border:none;border-radius:10px;' +
        'padding:12px 20px;font-weight:bold;font-size:15px;cursor:pointer;width:100%;margin-bottom:10px';

      closeBtn.onclick = function(){ overlay.remove(); };
      card.appendChild(title); card.appendChild(body); card.appendChild(getBtn); card.appendChild(closeBtn);
      overlay.appendChild(card);

    }
    // Exposed so GDScript (Main.gd's Connect Wallet handlers) can trigger the
    // exact same popup via JavaScriptBridge.eval when there's no provider —
    // one popup, one set of store links, instead of duplicating this in Godot.
    window._showNimiqInstallPopup = showInstallPopup;

    function showBanner() {
      if (insideNimiqPay()) return;
      var banner=document.createElement('div');
      banner.id='nq-banner';
      banner.style.cssText='position:fixed;top:0;left:0;right:0;z-index:99998;background:linear-gradient(90deg,#1a1a2e,#16213e);color:#fff;display:flex;align-items:center;justify-content:space-between;padding:10px 14px;font-family:sans-serif;font-size:14px;box-shadow:0 2px 8px rgba(0,0,0,.5);box-sizing:border-box';

      // Deferred-deep-link pattern: fire the custom-scheme link, then check
      // back in shortly — if the tab is still visible/foregrounded, the OS

      // happened, so show the install popup instead of leaving the button
      // looking like it did nothing at all.
      open.onclick=function(){

        setTimeout(function(){
```
