```html
      };
      var cls=document.createElement('button');
      cls.textContent='✕';
      cls.style.cssText='background:transparent;color:#aaa;border:none;font-size:18px;cursor:pointer;margin-left:8px;padding:0 4px;flex-shrink:0';
      cls.onclick=function(){
        banner.style.display='none';
        try{sessionStorage.setItem('nq_banner_dismissed','1');}catch(e){}
      };
      banner.appendChild(txt); banner.appendChild(open); banner.appendChild(cls);
      if (document.body) document.body.appendChild(banner);
      else document.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded',function(){document.body.appendChild(banner);});
    }

    // ── AUTO-REDIRECT when the URL already carries params ───────────────────
    // If the page was opened with query params (e.g. <game url>?vs=id —
    // a referral/session id that should drive an automatic NIM
    // payout), don't make the player notice+tap the top banner's "Open"
    // button first. Jump straight to a centered "Opening Nimiq Pay…" popup
    // AND fire the deep link immediately, in the background, on load. The
    // popup stays up as visible confirmation something is happening (and as
    // a manual fallback button) while window.location.href does its thing;
    // same deferred-deep-link check as the banner's button (still visible
    // after ~1.2s -> Nimiq Pay isn't installed -> swap to the install
    // popup) so a player without the app doesn't just see a popup that
    // silently never resolves.
    function hasForwardableParams() {
      try { return window.location.search.length > 1; } catch(e) { return false; }
    }
    function showAutoRedirectPopup() {
      if (document.getElementById('nq-auto-redirect')) return;
      var overlay = document.createElement('div');
      overlay.id = 'nq-auto-redirect';
      overlay.style.cssText = 'position:fixed;inset:0;z-index:99999;background:rgba(0,0,0,.6);' +
        'display:flex;align-items:center;justify-content:center;font-family:sans-serif;padding:24px;box-sizing:border-box';
      var card = document.createElement('div');
      card.style.cssText = 'background:#1a1a2e;color:#fff;border-radius:16px;padding:24px;max-width:340px;' +
        'width:100%;text-align:center;box-shadow:0 8px 32px rgba(0,0,0,.5)';
      var title = document.createElement('div');
      title.textContent = 'Opening Nimiq Pay…';
      title.style.cssText = 'font-size:18px;font-weight:bold;margin-bottom:10px';
      var body = document.createElement('div');
      body.textContent = "Taking you to Nimiq Pay to claim your NIM reward. If nothing happens, tap below.";
      body.style.cssText = 'font-size:14px;line-height:1.4;color:#cfd0e0;margin-bottom:18px';
      var openBtn = document.createElement('button');
      openBtn.textContent = 'Open Nimiq Pay ↗';
      openBtn.style.cssText = 'background:#f6b221;color:#1a1a2e;border:none;border-radius:10px;' +
        'padding:12px 20px;font-weight:bold;font-size:15px;cursor:pointer;width:100%;margin-bottom:10px';
      openBtn.onclick = function(){ if (DEEP_LINK) window.location.href = DEEP_LINK; };
      var closeBtn = document.createElement('button');
      closeBtn.textContent = 'Continue on web';
      closeBtn.style.cssText = 'background:transparent;color:#9a9ab0;border:none;font-size:14px;cursor:pointer;padding:6px';
      closeBtn.onclick = function(){
        overlay.remove();
        try { sessionStorage.setItem('nq_banner_dismissed', '1'); } catch(e) {}
      };
      card.appendChild(title); card.appendChild(body); card.appendChild(openBtn); card.appendChild(closeBtn);
      overlay.appendChild(card);
      // No backdrop-tap-to-dismiss here (unlike showInstallPopup/showBanner)
      // — this popup represents an in-flight automatic action the player
      // didn't have to ask for, an accidental tap outside it shouldn't
      // silently cancel the payout attempt. "Continue on web" is the
      // explicit, intentional way out.
      document.body.appendChild(overlay);
    }
    function tryAutoRedirect() {
      if (!hasForwardableParams() || insideNimiqPay() || !DEEP_LINK) return false;
      // BUG FIX: the very first insideNimiqPay() check above can run before
      // the native host has actually injected window.nimiqPay yet (that
      // check above is synchronous, right at load) — the flag can still
      // land a beat later. Firing the popup+redirect immediately on that
      // false negative, then correcting a moment later once the flag shows
      // up, is exactly what caused the "Open Nimiq Pay" popup to flash on
      // screen for a fraction of a second and then vanish — technically
      // correct (nothing wrong happened, no incorrect install-prompt), but
      // visually looks like a glitch. Fix: give window.nimiqPay a brief,
      // silent grace window (300ms, checked every 50ms) to show up BEFORE
      // we ever create the popup or touch window.location — a real "not
      // inside Nimiq Pay" case barely feels the extra 300ms, but a
      // just-opened-inside-Nimiq-Pay case never sees the popup flash at all.
      var _checks = 0, _maxChecks = 6; // 6 * 50ms = 300ms
      var _grace = setInterval(function(){
        _checks++;
        if (insideNimiqPay()) { clearInterval(_grace); return; } // confirmed inside within the grace window -> do nothing, no flash
        if (_checks >= _maxChecks) {
          clearInterval(_grace);
          showAutoRedirectPopup();
          window.location.href = DEEP_LINK;
          setTimeout(function(){
            // Re-check once more before falling back to the install popup —
            // same reasoning as above, just a second, later checkpoint.
            if (insideNimiqPay()) {
              var already = document.getElementById('nq-auto-redirect');
              if (already) already.remove();
              return;
            }
            if (document.visibilityState === 'visible') {
              var el = document.getElementById('nq-auto-redirect');
              if (el) el.remove();
              showInstallPopup();
            }
          }, 1200);
        }
      }, 50);
      return true;
    }
    // Params present -> ALSO kick off the auto-redirect popup, but this
    // must NOT skip the banner logic below — the banner ("Play in Nimiq
    // Pay & earn 2x NIM rewards") stays the one always-on signal whenever
    // we're not inside Nimiq Pay, param or no param. The two are additive,
    // not either/or.
    if (hasForwardableParams()) {
      if (document.body) tryAutoRedirect();
      else document.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', tryAutoRedirect);
    }

    // Wait for the SDK's definitive result instead of guessing off a fixed delay.
    // _initNimiq starts ~3.5s after load and sdk.init() itself can take up to 10s,
    // so worst case this can take up to ~15s — that's fine, it's the correct signal.
    // A generous ceiling is kept only as a safety net in case the SDK hangs/never
    // resolves (e.g. blocked network); in that edge case we fall back to showing.
    var MAX_WAIT_MS = 16000, STEP_MS = 100, waited = 0;
    var poll = setInterval(function() {
      waited += STEP_MS;
      if (insideNimiqPay()) { clearInterval(poll); return; }               // confirmed: inside -> never show
      if (providerConfirmedMissing()) { clearInterval(poll); showBanner(); return; } // confirmed: not inside -> show now
      if (waited >= MAX_WAIT_MS) { clearInterval(poll); showBanner(); }    // safety-net fallback
    }, STEP_MS);
  })();
  </script>

</head>

<!-- BUG FIX (game shows briefly then goes black after rotating back to
     portrait): removing display:none from #canvas (see the media query in
     <style> above) fixed the WebGL-context-loss black screen, but exposed
     a SECOND bug — #canvas is no longer display:none while landscape, so
     its CSS box now actually grows to the real landscape width/height
     (still fully hidden behind the opaque #rotate-lock overlay, but Godot
     doesn't know that). Godot's own default canvasResizePolicy watches the
     canvas element's real size and resizes its internal viewport/
     framebuffer to match on every 'resize' — so it now genuinely resizes
     itself into a landscape framebuffer while rotated, then resizes AGAIN
     back to portrait a moment later. Main.gd's landscape-restriction logic
     was deliberately disabled (_check_landscape() is a no-op — see that
     function's comment), meaning nothing in GDScript ever validated that a
     landscape-shaped viewport actually renders correctly — it doesn't:
     the brief "comes back, then goes black" is that bad landscape resize
     round-trip landing the renderer in a broken state.

     Fix: keep #canvas's CSS box PINNED at its last known portrait size for
     the entire time the device is physically in landscape, so neither
     Godot's engine.js nor Main.gd's _on_viewport_resized() ever sees a
     landscape-shaped viewport at all — same end goal the old display:none
     approach had ("the canvas never sees a landscape size"), just without
     touching display, so the WebGL context is never freed either.

     BUG FIX #2 (safe-area padding sometimes wrong/stale after rotating
     back): Main.gd's own _on_viewport_resized() is the ONLY thing that
     calls _refresh_safe_area_bottom() on a rotation (see that function —
     "rotasyonda safe-area değişebilir... bar/HUD reposition dahil"), and
     Godot only fires that signal when the canvas's REAL measured size
     actually changes. Freezing #canvas at the exact same pixel size the
     whole way through a rotate-away-and-back cycle (the fix directly
     above) means Godot now sees NO size change at all across the whole
     cycle — so it never re-fires _on_viewport_resized(), so
     _refresh_safe_area_bottom() never re-runs, so Main.gd keeps whatever
     _safe_area_bottom value it had before the rotation even if the real
     env(safe-area-inset-*) changed (landscape can have a different safe
     area than portrait on notched phones, and JS's own
     window._lastSafeAreaSignals — read by _refresh_safe_area_bottom() —
     DOES keep updating live off the real env() values the whole time,
     completely independent of our pin/unpin, since it doesn't measure the
     canvas at all). Net effect: JS has the right numbers ready, but
     nothing ever tells Godot to go read them again.
     Fix: once back in portrait, force ONE genuine, Godot-visible resize —
     nudge the canvas 1px narrower, let the browser paint that (two
     requestAnimationFrame callbacks, so the resize-observer/next-frame
     watcher Godot's shell uses definitely sees it as a real, separate
     size), then restore the exact real size. Two real size changes back
     to back — Godot's own vp.size_changed fires normally off the second
     one, which runs its EXISTING _on_viewport_resized() →
     _refresh_safe_area_bottom() path with fresh, correct, already-settled
     env() values. No GDScript changes needed; this only ever nudges
     AFTER we've confirmed the device is back in portrait, so the 1px
     blip is not visible during the landscape/rotate-lock window. -->
<script data-cfasync="false">
  (function () {
    var mq = window.matchMedia('(orientation: landscape) and (pointer: coarse) and (hover: none)');
    var canvas = document.getElementById('canvas');
    var statusEl = document.getElementById('status');
    var lockedW = 0, lockedH = 0;

    function captureSize() {
      if (!canvas) return;
      var r = canvas.getBoundingClientRect();
      if (r.width > 0 && r.height > 0) { lockedW = r.width; lockedH = r.height; }
    }

    function pin(el) {
      if (!el || lockedW <= 0 || lockedH <= 0) return;
      el.style.setProperty('width',  lockedW + 'px', 'important');
      el.style.setProperty('height', lockedH + 'px', 'important');
    }

    function unpin(el) {
      if (!el) return;
      el.style.removeProperty('width');
      el.style.removeProperty('height');
    }

    // Forces Godot to observe a real, two-step size change on `canvas` so
    // its own resize/safe-area refresh path runs — see BUG FIX #2 above.
    //
    // BUG FIX #2b: changing canvas.style.width/height alone does NOT make
    // Godot notice anything — Godot's own resize handling (same as the
    // existing syncCanvasBackingStore() code elsewhere in this file, see
    // its "A synthetic 'resize' is ... exactly what tells Godot to re-read
    // the canvas" comment) is driven off the window 'resize' event, not an
    // element-level observer. A plain style mutation fires no such event
    // by itself, so the first version of this fix silently did nothing —
    // Godot never re-read the nudged size, so _on_viewport_resized() (and
    // therefore _refresh_safe_area_bottom()) still never re-ran. Fix:
    // explicitly dispatch a synthetic 'resize' right after EACH of the two
    // size changes below, so Godot's listener actually fires each time and
    // picks up the temporarily-different size, then the corrected real one.
    //
    // #status doesn't need this: it's the loading splash, not something
    // Main.gd repositions off safe-area, and it's normally removed from
    // the DOM (setStatusMode('hidden') → .remove()) long before a player
    // could ever rotate their phone.
    function fireResize() { window.dispatchEvent(new Event('resize')); }

    function nudgeForRealResize() {
      if (!canvas) return;
      var r = canvas.getBoundingClientRect();
      if (r.width <= 1 || r.height <= 0) return; // nothing sane to nudge from
      var realW = r.width, realH = r.height;
      canvas.style.setProperty('width',  (realW - 1) + 'px', 'important');
      canvas.style.setProperty('height', realH + 'px', 'important');
      fireResize();
      requestAnimationFrame(function () {
        requestAnimationFrame(function () {
          // Restore the exact natural (calc-driven) size — removing the
          // override rather than re-setting realW/realH means it stays
          // correct even if the safe-area insets shifted again in the
          // one frame we waited (e.g. address bar finished animating).
          canvas.style.removeProperty('width');
          canvas.style.removeProperty('height');
          fireResize();
        });
      });
    }

    function apply(isLandscapeLocked) {
      if (isLandscapeLocked) {
        // Pin to whatever the last real portrait measurement was — taken
        // BEFORE this function ever runs with isLandscapeLocked=true, so
        // it's always a genuine portrait size, never a mid-rotation one.
        pin(canvas);
        pin(statusEl);
        fireResize(); // keep Godot in sync with the pinned (unchanged) size immediately, don't wait for its own listener to eventually catch up
      } else {
        unpin(canvas);
        unpin(statusEl);
        // Refresh the locked size now that we're confirmed back in
        // portrait, so the NEXT rotation pins to a fresh, current value
        // (handles the player resizing the browser/PWA window, or a
        // different portrait size after an OS UI change, between rotations).
        captureSize();
        nudgeForRealResize();
      }
    }

    captureSize();
    apply(mq.matches);
    if (mq.addEventListener) mq.addEventListener('change', function (e) { apply(e.matches); });
    else mq.addListener(function (e) { apply(e.matches); }); // Safari <14 fallback
  })();
</script>

<!-- Best-effort real lock for browsers/PWA contexts that support it (mostly
     Android Chrome when installed to home screen). Wrapped in try/catch —
     silently does nothing where unsupported (e.g. plain iOS Safari tabs),
     which is fine since the CSS #rotate-lock above covers those cases. -->
<script data-cfasync="false">
  (function () {
    function tryLock() {
      try {
        if (screen.orientation && screen.orientation.lock) {
          // GYRO-AXIS BUG FIX: the W3C Screen Orientation API's 'portrait'
          // lock type is NOT "upright portrait only" — per spec it means
          // "portrait-primary OR portrait-secondary", i.e. it explicitly
          // PERMITS the OS to rotate the canvas into upside-down portrait
          // (portrait-secondary) on any browser context that actually
          // honors this call (per the comment above, mostly Android
          // Chrome PWA/installed contexts). The CSS #rotate-lock blocker
          // below doesn't catch this either — its media query only fires
          // on `orientation: landscape`, and upside-down portrait is still
          // `orientation: portrait` as far as CSS is concerned. If the OS
          // actually rotates into portrait-secondary, the canvas gets
          // visually flipped 180° to compensate (correct, expected
          // behavior for a real orientation lock) — but devicemotion's
          // accelerationIncludingGravity is reported in the device's raw
          // HARDWARE frame, which is never rotated by the OS/CSS
          // transform. So a player holding the phone upside-down would
          // see a correctly-upright (rotated) canvas, tap zones that
          // still work (touch coordinates ARE compensated for the CSS
          // rotation), but gyro left/right permanently reversed, because
          // the raw acc.x sign convention this code relies on (see
          // Main.gd's _startGyroListener) assumes portrait-primary only.
          // 'portrait-primary' locks to just the single upright
          // orientation and prevents the OS from ever rotating into
          // portrait-secondary in the first place, closing this off at
          // the source instead of trying to compensate for it later.
          screen.orientation.lock('portrait-primary').catch(function () {});
        }
      } catch (e) {}
    }
    tryLock();
    document.addEventListener('visibilitychange', tryLock);
  })();
</script>

  <progress id="status-progress"></progress>
  <div id="status-notice"></div>
</div>

<!-- ── ERROR CAPTURE + BACKEND LOG FLUSH ─────────────────────────────────────
     Always active: catches errors silently and batches them to /backend/client-log.
     DEV mode adds: visible overlay, copy button, FPS counter.
─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── -->
<script data-cfasync="false">
(function(){
  var DEV = window._DEV;

  // ── Dev overlay (only in ?dev mode) ──────────────────────────────────────
  var _log = function(){}; // no-op in prod
  if (DEV) {
    var box=document.createElement('div');
    box.style.cssText='position:fixed;bottom:44px;left:0;right:0;max-height:60vh;overflow-y:auto;background:rgba(0,0,0,.95);color:#0f0;font:11px monospace;z-index:99999;padding:4px;display:none';
    document.body.appendChild(box);

    var btn=document.createElement('button');
    btn.textContent='🐛';
    btn.style.cssText='position:fixed;bottom:4px;right:6px;z-index:100000;background:#333;color:#fff;border:none;border-radius:50%;width:36px;height:36px;font-size:18px;cursor:pointer';
    btn.onclick=function(){box.style.display=box.style.display==='none'?'block':'none';box.scrollTop=box.scrollHeight;};
    document.body.appendChild(btn);

    var copyBtn=document.createElement('button');
    copyBtn.textContent='📋';
    copyBtn.style.cssText='position:fixed;bottom:4px;right:48px;z-index:100000;background:#444;color:#fff;border:none;border-radius:50%;width:36px;height:36px;font-size:16px;cursor:pointer';
    var _lines=[];
    copyBtn.onclick=function(){
      var txt=_lines.join('\n');
      if(navigator.clipboard){navigator.clipboard.writeText(txt);}
      else{var ta=document.createElement('textarea');ta.value=txt;document.body.appendChild(ta);ta.select();document.execCommand('copy');document.body.removeChild(ta);}
      copyBtn.textContent='✓';setTimeout(function(){copyBtn.textContent='📋';},1500);
    };
    document.body.appendChild(copyBtn);

    _log = function(msg, color) {
      var line = new Date().toISOString().slice(11,19)+' '+msg;
      _lines.push(line);
      var d=document.createElement('div');
      d.textContent=line;
      d.style.cssText='border-bottom:1px solid #111;padding:1px 0;color:'+(color||'#0f0');
      box.appendChild(d);
      if(_lines.length>500){_lines.shift();if(box.firstChild)box.removeChild(box.firstChild);}
      box.scrollTop=box.scrollHeight;
    };

    // FPS monitor (dev only)
    var _ff=0,_fl=performance.now(),_fp=0,_fw=0,_fs=0;
    function _fpsCount(){
      var now=performance.now(),ft=now-_fp;_fp=now;
      if(ft>0&&ft<500){_fs+=ft;if(ft>_fw)_fw=ft;}_ff++;
      if(now-_fl>=5000){
        _log('FPS='+Math.round(_ff*1000/(now-_fl))+' avgFT='+Math.round(_fs/_ff)+'ms worstFT='+Math.round(_fw)+'ms');
        _ff=0;_fl=now;_fw=0;_fs=0;
      }
      requestAnimationFrame(_fpsCount);
    }
    requestAnimationFrame(_fpsCount);

    // Device info on start
    _log('UA: '+navigator.userAgent.slice(0,100));
    _log('DPR='+window.devicePixelRatio+' screen='+screen.width+'x'+screen.height);
    _log('hwConcurrency='+navigator.hardwareConcurrency);
  }

  // expose for game engine init below
  window._earlyLog = _log;

  // _enqueue itself is exposed further down, right after it's defined —
  // see window._enqueueLog below.

  // ── Backend log queue ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  var _queue = [];
  var _timer = null;
  // BUG FIX: this used to be the relative path '/backend/client-log', which
  // resolves against the PAGE's own origin (window.location.origin). In the
  // default deployment the game's static files and the Go backend are on two
  // DIFFERENT domains (game_url vs api_base in setup/urls.ini), with no
  // reverse-proxy making <game url>/backend/* reach the backend — so every
  // request 404'd against the game's own static host. Fix: resolve the same
  // base URL ApiConfig.gd uses (window.NJ_API_BASE > query param ?api= >
  // localStorage nj_api_base > the build-time api_base), so this always hits
  // the real backend regardless of which domain served the page.
  //
  // BUG FIX #2: devtools (start-dev-tunnels.js) overrides ApiConfig.gd's
  // PROD_BASE for every Godot-side network call, but this block runs in
  // plain JS before/alongside the engine and never shared that override —
  // it only ever checked ?api=/localStorage, which nothing actually sets, so
  // every /backend/client-log POST during a devtools tunnel test kept going
  // to the hardcoded prod fallback below and got CORS-rejected (prod's
  // allowlist doesn't know the tunnel origin). window.NJ_API_BASE closes
  // that gap: devtools' frontend static server now injects it directly into
  // this served index.html with the current backend tunnel URL (see
  // injectApiBase() in start-dev-tunnels.js) — checked first, before the
  // query param / localStorage fallbacks, which remain for the case of
  // manually testing against a non-default backend without devtools.
  var _API_BASE = (function(){
    try {
      if (window.NJ_API_BASE) return String(window.NJ_API_BASE).replace(/\/+$/, '');
    } catch(e) {}
    try {
      var q = new URLSearchParams(window.location.search).get('api');
      if (q) return q.replace(/\/+$/, '');
    } catch(e) {}
    try {
      var ls = window.localStorage && window.localStorage.getItem('nj_api_base');
      if (ls) return ls.replace(/\/+$/, '');
    } catch(e) {}
    // Placeholder — setup/build.py substitutes the api_base from
    // setup/urls.ini here, the same value apply_urls.py writes into
    // ApiConfig.gd's PROD_BASE. Nothing to keep in sync by hand.
    return '__API_BASE__'.replace(/\/+$/, '');
  })();
  var _BACKEND = _API_BASE + '/backend/client-log';

  function _deviceMeta() {
    return {
      user_agent: (navigator.userAgent||'').slice(0,200),
      screen:     screen.width+'x'+screen.height,
      platform:   (navigator.userAgentData&&navigator.userAgentData.platform)||navigator.platform||'',
      dpr:        String(window.devicePixelRatio||1)
    };
  }

  function _flush() {
    if (!_queue.length) return;
    var batch = _queue.splice(0, 30);
    var payload = Object.assign({ entries: batch }, _deviceMeta());
    var headers = { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' };
    var tok = window._nimiqAuthToken || '';
    if (tok) headers['Authorization'] = 'Bearer '+tok;
    var body = JSON.stringify(payload);
    // BUG FIX: this used to silently swallow every failure with no retry.
    // In devtools tunnel testing, the very first POST here (this fires
    // before Godot/wasm even loads) can land on Cloudflare's edge before a
    // freshly-created Quick Tunnel has fully settled, getting a 502 with no
    // CORS headers — a transient infra blip, not a real failure. One quiet
    // retry after a short delay avoids losing that entry outright; still a
    // no-op fire-and-forget after that (this is a write-only diagnostic
    // sink, never worth bothering the player about).
    fetch(_BACKEND, { method:'POST', headers:headers, body:body, keepalive:true })
      .catch(function(){
        setTimeout(function(){
          fetch(_BACKEND, { method:'POST', headers:headers, body:body, keepalive:true }).catch(function(){});
        }, 800);
      });
  }

  function _enqueue(level, msg) {
    _queue.push({ level:level, message:msg });
    if (_queue.length >= 30) { clearTimeout(_timer); _timer=null; _flush(); return; }
    // Any "error" in the queue gets a short debounce (250ms — still batches
    // a burst of errors from the same crash into one request) instead of
    // waiting up to 30s like pure warn/info. Reasoning: if the page/webview
    // gets killed abruptly right after an error (very plausible here — this
    // runs inside Nimiq Pay's mini-app host, which can switch away from /
    // kill the tab with zero warning, unlike a normal desktop browser tab
    // close), anything still sitting in the 30s-debounced queue never
    // reaches the backend — no pagehide/visibilitychange fires either,
    // since the host isn't giving the page a normal close. Recomputed from
    // the whole queue's contents (not just this call's level) so a warn
    // arriving right after a queued error can't push the error's flush back
    // out to the slow 30s timer.
    var hasError = false;
    for (var i = 0; i < _queue.length; i++) { if (_queue[i].level === 'error') { hasError = true; break; } }
    var delayMs = hasError ? 250 : 30000;
    clearTimeout(_timer);
    _timer = setTimeout(function(){ _timer=null; _flush(); }, delayMs);
  }
  // Exposed so the separate Engine-bootstrap <script> block further down
  // (which runs in its own IIFE/scope, can't see this one's locals) can
  // report the capability probe / missing-features result through the same
  // queue/backend-flush machinery instead of duplicating it.
  window._enqueueLog = _enqueue;

  document.addEventListener('visibilitychange', function(){ if(document.visibilityState==='hidden') _flush(); });
  window.addEventListener('pagehide', _flush);

  // ── Error hooks ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  var _ol=console.log.bind(console), _ow=console.warn.bind(console), _oe=console.error.bind(console);

  window.onerror = function(msg, src, line, col, err) {
    var m = String(msg).slice(0,300)+' @'+String(src).slice(-60)+':'+line;
    if (DEV) { _log('❌ '+m, '#f55'); if(err&&err.stack) _log('  '+err.stack.slice(0,200),'#f88'); box.style.display='block'; }
    _enqueue('error', m);
    return false;
  };
  window.addEventListener('unhandledrejection', function(e) {
    var r=e.reason, m='REJECT: '+((r&&(r.message||String(r)))||'?').slice(0,300);
    if (DEV) { _log('❌ '+m,'#f88'); if(r&&r.stack)_log('  '+r.stack.slice(0,200),'#f88'); box.style.display='block'; }
    _enqueue('error', m);
  });
  window.addEventListener('error', function(e) {
    var t=e.target;
    if (t && t!==window && t.tagName) {
      var url=t.src||t.href||'?';
      var m='RESOURCE_FAIL: <'+t.tagName.toLowerCase()+'> '+String(url).slice(-200);
      if (DEV) { _log('❌ '+m,'#f55'); box.style.display='block'; }
      _enqueue('error', m);
    }
  }, true);
  window.addEventListener('securitypolicyviolation', function(e) {
    var m='CSP: '+e.violatedDirective+' blocked='+String(e.blockedURI).slice(0,150);
    if (DEV) { _log('⚠ '+m,'#f80'); box.style.display='block'; }
    _enqueue('warn', m);
  });

  // Override console only in dev (avoid overhead in prod)
  if (DEV) {
    console.log   = function(){ var m=Array.prototype.join.call(arguments,' '); _log(m.slice(0,200)); _ol.apply(console,arguments); };
    console.warn  = function(){ var m=Array.prototype.join.call(arguments,' '); _log('⚠ '+m.slice(0,200),'#ff0'); _enqueue('warn',m.slice(0,300)); _ow.apply(console,arguments); };
    console.error = function(){ var m=Array.prototype.join.call(arguments,' '); _log('❌ '+m.slice(0,200),'#f55'); _enqueue('error',m.slice(0,300)); box.style.display='block'; _oe.apply(console,arguments); };
  }
  // In prod, still capture console.error/warn to backend
  else {
    console.warn  = function(){ _enqueue('warn',  Array.prototype.join.call(arguments,' ').slice(0,300)); _ow.apply(console,arguments); };
    console.error = function(){ _enqueue('error', Array.prototype.join.call(arguments,' ').slice(0,300)); _oe.apply(console,arguments); };
  }
})();
</script>

<!-- ── REPLAY DEBUG INTERCEPTOR ───────────────────────────────────────────── -->
<!-- Sadece ?dev modunda aktif. Godot print() çıktılarını ve replay flow'unu izler. -->
<script data-cfasync="false">
(function() {
  if (!window._DEV) return;

  // Godot engine print() → JS console bridge
  // Engine başladıktan sonra stdout'u yakala
  var _origPrint = window.print;
  Object.defineProperty(window, 'print', {
    set: function(fn) {
      _origPrint = fn;
      window._gdPrint = function(msg) {
        if (typeof msg === 'string' && (
          msg.indexOf('[STATS]') !== -1 ||
          msg.indexOf('[LB]') !== -1 ||
          msg.indexOf('replay') !== -1 ||
          msg.indexOf('REPLAY') !== -1 ||
          msg.indexOf('block_lb') !== -1 ||
          msg.indexOf('_started') !== -1
        )) {
          window._earlyLog && window._earlyLog('🎮 ' + msg.slice(0, 200), '#0ff');
        }
        fn(msg);
      };
    },
    get: function() { return _origPrint; },
    configurable: true
  });

  // Fetch interceptor — tüm /backend/replay/* isteklerini logla
  var _origFetch = window.fetch;
  window.fetch = function(url, opts) {
    var urlStr = String(url);
    if (urlStr.indexOf('/backend/replay') !== -1 ||
        urlStr.indexOf('/backend/stats') !== -1 ||
        urlStr.indexOf('/backend/leaderboard') !== -1) {
      var method = (opts && opts.method) || 'GET';
      window._earlyLog && window._earlyLog('📡 FETCH ' + method + ' ' + urlStr.slice(0, 120), '#0af');
      return _origFetch.apply(this, arguments).then(function(r) {
        window._earlyLog && window._earlyLog(
          '📡 RESP ' + r.status + ' ' + urlStr.slice(urlStr.lastIndexOf('/'), urlStr.lastIndexOf('/') + 40),
          r.ok ? '#0f0' : '#f55'
        );
        return r;
      }).catch(function(e) {
        window._earlyLog && window._earlyLog('📡 ERR ' + urlStr.slice(0,80) + ' → ' + e.message, '#f55');
        throw e;
      });
    }
    return _origFetch.apply(this, arguments);
  };

  // XMLHttpRequest interceptor (Godot HTTPRequest uses XHR on web)
  var _XHROpen = XMLHttpRequest.prototype.open;
  var _XHRSend = XMLHttpRequest.prototype.send;
  XMLHttpRequest.prototype.open = function(method, url) {
    this._dbgUrl = String(url);
    this._dbgMethod = method;
    return _XHROpen.apply(this, arguments);
  };
  XMLHttpRequest.prototype.send = function() {
    var url = this._dbgUrl || '';
    if (url.indexOf('/backend/replay') !== -1 ||
        url.indexOf('/backend/stats') !== -1 ||
        url.indexOf('/backend/leaderboard') !== -1) {
      var self = this;
      window._earlyLog && window._earlyLog('🌐 XHR ' + (this._dbgMethod||'?') + ' ' + url.slice(0, 120), '#0af');
      this.addEventListener('load', function() {
        window._earlyLog && window._earlyLog(
          '🌐 XHR ' + self.status + ' ' + url.slice(url.lastIndexOf('/'), url.lastIndexOf('/') + 50),
          self.status === 200 ? '#0f0' : '#f55'
        );
        if (self.status === 200 && url.indexOf('/replay/') !== -1) {
          try {
            var d = JSON.parse(self.responseText);
            window._earlyLog && window._earlyLog(
              '✅ REPLAY DATA: seed=' + d.seed + ' has_log=' + (!!d.replay_log) +
              ' log_len=' + (d.replay_log ? d.replay_log.length : 0) +
              ' char=' + d.char + ' player_seed=' + d.player_seed, '#0f0');
          } catch(e) {
            window._earlyLog && window._earlyLog('⚠ REPLAY JSON parse fail: ' + e.message, '#f80');
          }
        }
      });
      this.addEventListener('error', function() {
        window._earlyLog && window._earlyLog('🌐 XHR ERROR ' + url.slice(0, 80), '#f55');
      });
    }
    return _XHRSend.apply(this, arguments);
  };

  window._earlyLog && window._earlyLog('🐛 Replay debug interceptor aktif', '#ff0');
})();
</script>

<!-- ── GAME ENGINE LOADER ──────────────────────────────────────────────────── -->
<script data-cfasync="false">
(function() {
  var DEV = window._DEV;
  var gameUrl = "$GODOT_URL";
  if (DEV) window._earlyLog("⏳ Downloading game.js…");

  fetch(gameUrl)
    .then(function(r){ if(!r.ok) throw new Error('HTTP '+r.status); return r.text(); })
    .then(function(code) {
      // Bypass Safari v15.2 check injected by Emscripten.
      //
      // Emscripten ships this check because of a real WebKit WASM bug that
      // existed before Safari 15.2 — it's not overcautious noise, it's a
      // guard against actual miscompiles/crashes on those older builds.
      // Whoever added this bypass presumably found it too aggressive for
      // some Safari version that in practice worked fine — but stripping it
      // unconditionally means ANY visitor still on a genuinely-affected
      // pre-15.2 Safari (this device's floor is iOS 15.0+ for WebGL2 to
      // begin with, so the exposed window here is specifically 15.0/15.1)
      // now attempts to run anyway. Instead of Emscripten's own clean "your
      // Safari is too old" error, they can hit the raw underlying WASM bug
      // directly — which looks like exactly this ticket: "game doesn't even
      // open," no clear error, nothing obviously wrong in a screenshot.
      // Not reverting this blind (don't know what specifically it was
      // fixing for whoever added it) — but this was previously only logged
      // in DEV, so there was literally no data on how often it fires in
      // production. Logging it for real now so the Logs tab can be
      // cross-referenced against the device-capability probe above (same
      // session, same timestamp) to see whether "won't open" reports
      // cluster on exactly this Safari version range.
      var p1=/throw\s+new\s+Error\(['"]This emscripten-generated code requires Safari v15.2.0.*?['"]\);?/g;
      if(p1.test(code)){
        code=code.replace(p1,'/* Safari check bypassed */');
        if(DEV) window._earlyLog("🎯 Safari throw removed");
        if (window._enqueueLog) window._enqueueLog('warn', 'SAFARI_BYPASS: pre-15.2 Safari check stripped, attempting run anyway — ' + navigator.userAgent.slice(0,150));
      }
      if(code.includes("requires Safari v15.2.0")){
        code=code.split('\n').map(function(l){
          return l.includes("requires Safari v15.2.0") ? "/* "+l+" */" : l;
        }).join('\n');
        if(DEV) window._earlyLog("🛡️ Safari line cleaned");
      }
      var s=document.createElement('script');
      s.text=code; s.setAttribute('data-cfasync','false');
      document.body.appendChild(s);
      window._godotEngineLoaded=true;
      if(window._startGodotSetup) window._startGodotSetup();
    })
    .catch(function(err){
      window._earlyLog && window._earlyLog('❌ game.js INJECT ERROR: '+err.message,'#f55');
    });
})();
</script>

<!-- ── GODOT ENGINE INIT ───────────────────────────────────────────────────── -->
<script data-cfasync="false">
function initGodotGame() {
  var DEV = window._DEV;
  var GODOT_CONFIG = $GODOT_CONFIG;
  GODOT_CONFIG['ensureCrossOriginIsolationHeaders'] = false;
  GODOT_CONFIG['serviceWorker'] = '';

  // Cap DPR at 1.5 to reduce GPU load on high-DPI screens.
  //
  // BUG FIX ("touches near the bottom bar land on the wrong Y on some
  // phones"): this used to run exactly once, right here, taking a single
  // getBoundingClientRect() snapshot and baking it into canvas.width/
  // height (the backing-store resolution Godot uses to map touch
  // coordinates). Every other height-dependent value in this file
  // (--app-height) got retries + a ResizeObserver + polling specifically
  // because that first snapshot can be wrong, and because "; wv)" Android
  // WebView sessions don't reliably fire resize/scroll afterward. This
  // snippet never got that treatment, so once the nav bar settled to its
  // real size (or appeared mid-session via Android's swipe-to-show
  // gesture bar) the backing store went stale relative to the visible
  // CSS box and touch mapping drifted — worst right at the bottom strip
  // where Quests/Stats/Leaderboard/VS live.
  //
  // Fix: pull the sync into a standalone function, expose it as
  // window._syncCanvasBackingStore so the SAME retry/ResizeObserver/
  // polling machinery driving --app-height (see setAppHeight() in the
  // <head>) re-runs it too, and dispatch a synthetic 'resize' after any
  // change so Godot's own input/viewport handling picks up the new size
  // instead of only ever seeing the init-time one.
  (function() {
    function syncCanvasBackingStore() {
      var canvas = document.getElementById('canvas');
      if (!canvas) return;
      var rect = canvas.getBoundingClientRect();
      // Same guard as setAppHeight()'s h<=0 case: don't bake in a
      // snapshot taken before the WebView has actually laid out yet.
      // BUG FIX (rotation leaves the canvas zoomed into the top-left
      // corner): a rotate transition can momentarily report rect
      // width/height <= 0 (or an in-between size) mid-flip. This used to
      // `return` silently with NO retry scheduled, so if that was the
      // last resize-family event to fire, canvas.width/height stayed
      // wrong (or stale) forever — the CSS box then resizes to the
      // correct post-rotation size, but the backing store never gets
      // told to catch up, which is exactly "zoomed into the top-left and
      // stuck". Fix: schedule a short retry instead of giving up.
      // BUG FIX (WebGL "Could not create render target, status: 36054"
      // right at a rotation, engine then stuck/frozen): rect.width/height
      // can land on a tiny-but-nonzero value mid-transition (e.g. 1-2px),
      // which the old `<= 0` guard let straight through. Math.round(1 *
      // dpr) still produces a valid-looking but near-zero backing store
      // size; Godot then tries to build a render target/framebuffer at
      // that size and GLES3 rejects it (status 36054 /
      // GL_FRAMEBUFFER_INCOMPLETE_DIMENSIONS-class error), leaving the
      // renderer in a broken state that a later correct-size resize
      // event doesn't necessarily recover from — matches the "rotate and
      // it's stuck zoomed into the corner" report exactly. Raise the
      // floor from 0 to a real minimum so a garbage in-between frame is
      // treated the same as the <=0 case: skipped and retried, never
      // written to the canvas.
      var MIN_BACKING_PX = 32;
      if (rect.width <= 0 || rect.height <= 0 || rect.width < MIN_BACKING_PX || rect.height < MIN_BACKING_PX) {
        if (!syncCanvasBackingStore._retryQueued) {
          syncCanvasBackingStore._retryQueued = true;
          setTimeout(function () {
            syncCanvasBackingStore._retryQueued = false;
            syncCanvasBackingStore();
          }, 100);
        }
        return;
      }
      var dpr = Math.min(window.devicePixelRatio || 1, 1.5);
      var newW = Math.round(rect.width * dpr);
      var newH = Math.round(rect.height * dpr);
      if (canvas.width === newW && canvas.height === newH) return;
      canvas.width = newW;
      canvas.height = newH;
      if (DEV) window._earlyLog('Canvas backing store synced: ' + newW + 'x' + newH + ' (dpr=' + dpr.toFixed(2) + ', native=' + (window.devicePixelRatio || 1).toFixed(2) + ')');
      // Nudge the engine: Godot's viewport/input code derives its touch-
      // to-game-coordinate ratio from canvas.width/height vs. the CSS
      // box, but only recomputes it in response to a resize signal, not
      // by polling the canvas element itself. A synthetic 'resize' is a
      // no-op for setAppHeight()'s own equality check (the CSS box
      // hasn't changed) but is exactly what tells Godot to re-read the
      // canvas and stop mapping touches against the stale ratio.
      window.dispatchEvent(new Event('resize'));
      // BUG FIX cont'd: a size caught mid-transition can still be
      // "valid" (>0) but not the FINAL post-rotation size (an
      // intermediate frame of a CSS rotate/layout transition). One more
      // re-check shortly after catches that case the same way
      // orientationchange's existing 300ms re-check does — but for
      // every trigger path, not just orientationchange.
      if (!syncCanvasBackingStore._settleQueued) {
        syncCanvasBackingStore._settleQueued = true;
        setTimeout(function () {
          syncCanvasBackingStore._settleQueued = false;
          syncCanvasBackingStore();
        }, 250);
      }
    }
    window._syncCanvasBackingStore = syncCanvasBackingStore;
    syncCanvasBackingStore();

    var canvas = document.getElementById('canvas');
    if (!canvas) return;
    // Diagnostic: catch real WebGL context-lost events. Won't catch a hard
    // process-level crash, but if the Firefox/webview crash is a recoverable
    // context loss rather than a full process kill, this finally gives us a
    // visible log line instead of a silent reload.
    //
    // No reload-recovery here on purpose: the actual trigger for this event
    // during normal play was the portrait-lock CSS hiding #canvas with
    // display:none while rotated to landscape (see the #rotate-lock media
    // query above) — fixed at the root by no longer doing that, so this
    // listener should now only ever fire for a genuine GPU/driver-level
    // loss, which is rare and worth just logging rather than silently
    // reloading the player's game out from under them.
    canvas.addEventListener('webglcontextlost', function(e){
      e.preventDefault();
      console.error('WEBGL_CONTEXT_LOST', e);
      if (window._earlyLog) window._earlyLog('❌ WEBGL_CONTEXT_LOST','#f55');
      if (window._enqueueLog) window._enqueueLog('error', 'WEBGL_CONTEXT_LOST');
    }, false);
  })();

  if (typeof Engine === 'undefined') {
    if(DEV) window._earlyLog('❌ Engine not found','#f55');
    return;
  }

  // Better WebGL context for WebView
  // NOTE: desynchronized:true is disabled on Firefox/Gecko AND on WebKit
  // (Safari engine). It skips compositor vsync to reduce input latency, but
  // on Gecko and on WebKit-based system webviews this has been the trigger
  // for a GPU process crash right at first-frame/framebuffer allocation,
  // which the browser then "recovers" from by silently reloading the page —
  // no JS error, no time to flush logs, just "loads to 100% then reloads
  // itself". Chrome/Blink tolerates it fine, hence the Chrome-works /
  // Firefox+Safari-crash split.
  //
  // BUG FIX: the previous check only matched literal Firefox
  // (/Firefox/i.test(ua)), which misses the actual majority of affected
  // sessions — on iOS, EVERY browser (Safari, Chrome-iOS/"CriOS",
  // Firefox-iOS/"FxiOS", and any in-app WKWebView such as Nimiq Pay's
  // mini-app host) runs on the WebKit engine under the hood, Apple requires
  // it platform-wide. So the old check left desynchronized:true ON for all
  // of those, and the GPU-crash-reload kept firing there — no UA string
  // ever contains "Firefox" but the browser itself is still WebKit.
  // Detect "is this WebKit" instead of "is this literally Firefox", plus
  // keep the standalone Gecko check for desktop/Android Firefox.
  var _ua = navigator.userAgent;
  var _isGecko = /Firefox/i.test(_ua) && !/Seamonkey/i.test(_ua);
  // Any Apple touch device (iPhone/iPad/iPod, plus iPadOS 13+ which reports
  // as "MacIntel" but exposes touch points) is WebKit-only at the engine
  // level regardless of what the UA's browser name claims.
  var _isAppleTouch = /iPad|iPhone|iPod/.test(_ua) ||
    (navigator.platform === 'MacIntel' && navigator.maxTouchPoints > 1);
  // Desktop Safari itself (not Chrome/Firefox spoofing as Safari — those
  // still include their own token even on Mac).
  var _isDesktopSafari = /^((?!chrome|android|crios|fxios|edg).)*safari/i.test(_ua);
  var _isWebKitCrashRisk = _isGecko || _isAppleTouch || _isDesktopSafari;
  var _origCtx=HTMLCanvasElement.prototype.getContext;
  HTMLCanvasElement.prototype.getContext=function(type,attrs){
    if(type==='webgl2'||type==='webgl'||type==='webgl-experimental'){
      attrs=Object.assign({
        powerPreference:'high-performance', desynchronized: !_isWebKitCrashRisk,
        preserveDrawingBuffer:false, antialias:false,
        depth:true, stencil:false, alpha:false,
      },attrs||{});
    }
    return _origCtx.call(this,type,attrs);
  };

  var engine=new Engine(GODOT_CONFIG);
  var statusOverlay =document.getElementById('status');
  var statusProgress=document.getElementById('status-progress');
  var statusNotice  =document.getElementById('status-notice');
  var initializing=true, statusMode='';

  function setStatusMode(mode) {
    if(statusMode===mode||!initializing) return;
    if(mode==='hidden'){statusOverlay.remove();initializing=false;return;}
    statusOverlay.style.visibility='visible';
    statusProgress.style.display=mode==='progress'?'block':'none';
    statusNotice.style.display  =mode==='notice'  ?'block':'none';
    statusMode=mode;
  }
  function displayFailureNotice(err) {
    console.error(err);
    statusNotice.innerHTML='An error occurred trying to run '+GODOT_CONFIG['executable']+':<br>'+err.message;
    setStatusMode('notice');
  }

  // ── Capability probe ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  // Godot 4's web export (gl_compatibility renderer) hard-requires WebGL2 —
  // there is no WebGL1 fallback anywhere in Godot 4 (unlike Godot 3's GLES2
  // export); this is an engine-level limitation, confirmed against Godot's
  // own docs/forum, not something any project-side code change can add back.
  // What we CAN do: know exactly who this excludes and see it in the admin
  // Logs tab, instead of guessing. This probe runs on EVERY load (not just
  // failures) so the full device population is visible, not only the ones
  // that fail — sent as "info" so it never gets lost/misread as an actual
  // error in the Logs tab's error count.
  function _probeCapabilities() {
    var webgl1 = false, webgl2 = false, renderer = '', vendor = '';
    try {
      var c1 = document.createElement('canvas');
      var gl1 = c1.getContext('webgl') || c1.getContext('experimental-webgl');
      webgl1 = !!gl1;
      var c2 = document.createElement('canvas');
      var gl2 = c2.getContext('webgl2');
      webgl2 = !!gl2;
      var gl = gl2 || gl1;
      if (gl) {
        var dbg = gl.getExtension('WEBGL_debug_renderer_info');
        if (dbg) {
          renderer = String(gl.getParameter(dbg.UNMASKED_RENDERER_WEBGL) || '').slice(0, 100);
          vendor   = String(gl.getParameter(dbg.UNMASKED_VENDOR_WEBGL)   || '').slice(0, 60);
        }
      }
    } catch (e) { /* probing itself must never throw */ }
    var mem = (navigator.deviceMemory != null) ? (navigator.deviceMemory + 'GB') : '?';
    var cores = navigator.hardwareConcurrency || '?';
    var msg = 'CAPS webgl1=' + webgl1 + ' webgl2=' + webgl2 +
      ' gpu=' + (vendor || '?') + '/' + (renderer || '?') +
      ' mem=' + mem + ' cores=' + cores;
    if (DEV) window._earlyLog(msg, '#0ff');
    if (window._enqueueLog) window._enqueueLog('info', msg);
    return { webgl1: webgl1, webgl2: webgl2 };
  }
  var _caps = _probeCapabilities();

  // Cross-origin isolation check — kept as an informational log only.
  // crossOriginIsolated is EXPECTED to read false now: backend/main.go's
  // corsMiddleware deliberately relaxed Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy from
  // "same-origin" to "same-origin-allow-popups" (see that file's comment) to
  // fix the Nimiq Hub API's web sign-in popup, which strict COOP was
  // silently breaking ("Invalid Request" from hub.nimiq.com — same-origin
  // severs window.opener for any popup this page opens, which is exactly how
  // Hub's popup talks back to us). Relaxing COOP alone wasn't enough though —
  // Cross-Origin-Embedder-Policy: require-corp had to be removed too, since a
  // cross-origin-isolated page (COOP + COEP together) can't retain
  // window.opener on ANY cross-origin popup regardless of the COOP value.
  // That trade-off costs crossOriginIsolated/
  // SharedArrayBuffer, which this project's export never actually needed —
  // see Engine.getMissingFeatures({threads:false}) below and
  // GODOT_CONFIG['ensureCrossOriginIsolationHeaders']=false. Logged once, up
  // front, purely so a LOAD_STALL report can still be cross-referenced
  // against this if a *future* build ever does add a threaded export.
  var _coi = !!window.crossOriginIsolated;
  var _sab = (typeof SharedArrayBuffer !== 'undefined');
  var _coiMsg = 'COI crossOriginIsolated=' + _coi + ' SharedArrayBuffer=' + _sab;
  if (DEV) window._earlyLog(_coiMsg, '#0ff');
  if (window._enqueueLog) window._enqueueLog('info', _coiMsg);

  // ── Safe-area verification ────────────────────────────────────────────
  // The CSS env(safe-area-inset-*) fix on #canvas/#status (see <style>
  // above) can't be confirmed from here without an actual notched/home-
  // indicator device — logging the REAL computed inset values (in px) for
  // every session means the very first player who opens this on an iPhone
  // with a notch/Dynamic Island shows up in the admin Logs tab with actual
  // non-zero numbers, which is the only real proof the fix is doing
  // anything in production. All-zero on every session just means nobody
  // with a notch/home-indicator has opened it yet (or a device where the
  // safe area truly is zero, e.g. most Android phones) — not that the fix
  // is broken. Read via a throwaway element instead of trusting env()
  // support detection, since that's the only way to get the resolved px
  // value out of CSS into JS at all.
  function _probeSafeArea() {
    try {
      var probe = document.createElement('div');
      probe.style.cssText = 'position:fixed;top:0;left:0;visibility:hidden;pointer-events:none;' +
        'padding-top:env(safe-area-inset-top,0px);padding-bottom:env(safe-area-inset-bottom,0px);' +
        'padding-left:env(safe-area-inset-left,0px);padding-right:env(safe-area-inset-right,0px);';
      document.body.appendChild(probe);
      var cs = getComputedStyle(probe);
      var vals = { top: cs.paddingTop, bottom: cs.paddingBottom, left: cs.paddingLeft, right: cs.paddingRight };
      document.body.removeChild(probe);
      return vals;
    } catch (e) { return null; }
  }
  var _safeArea = _probeSafeArea();
  var _safeAreaMsg = _safeArea
    ? ('SAFE_AREA top=' + _safeArea.top + ' bottom=' + _safeArea.bottom + ' left=' + _safeArea.left + ' right=' + _safeArea.right)
    : 'SAFE_AREA probe-failed';
  if (DEV) window._earlyLog(_safeAreaMsg, '#0ff');
  if (window._enqueueLog) window._enqueueLog('info', _safeAreaMsg);

  // ── --app-height verification ───────────────────────────────────────
  // Same idea as the safe-area probe above, for the OTHER half of the
  // bottom-nav-bar-covered-by-OS-nav-bar fix: logs the gap (if any)
  // between the "naive" full CSS viewport and the real visualViewport-
  // derived height #canvas now actually uses. A non-zero gap on a
  // session confirms a device where the old 100%/100dvh-only sizing
  // would have drawn the canvas taller than what's really on screen
  // (Android nav bar, collapsed-toolbar edge case, etc.) — and that this
  // fix is the thing correcting it, not a coincidence.
  try {
    var _naiveH = window.innerHeight;
    var _realH  = window.visualViewport ? window.visualViewport.height : _naiveH;
    var _appHeightMsg = 'APP_HEIGHT naive=' + _naiveH + ' real=' + Math.round(_realH) +
      ' gap=' + Math.round(_naiveH - _realH);
    if (DEV) window._earlyLog(_appHeightMsg, '#0ff');
    if (window._enqueueLog) window._enqueueLog('info', _appHeightMsg);
  } catch (e) { /* logging itself must never throw */ }

  // ── SAFE AREA REPORT (on-screen panel) ──────────────────────────────
  // Measures every available signal and shows them in a small on-screen
  // panel (not just console) so this can be checked on any device
  // without a debugger attached. IMPORTANT: this file no longer decides
  // which signal is "the" answer — it only exposes the raw numbers via
  // window._lastSafeAreaSignals. Godot (Main.gd:_refresh_safe_area_bottom)
  // reads those raw numbers, applies its own plausibility filter, and
  // logs the chosen value to the admin panel — keeping the "which signal
  // do we trust" decision in one place instead of split between JS and
  // GDScript, which is what let a bad signal (e.g. an inflated
  // avail_vs_inner) get silently picked before.
  var SHOW_SAFE_AREA_PANEL = false; // flip to false to hide the on-screen panel
  function _measureSafeAreaSignals() {
    var out = {};
    try {
      var probe = document.createElement('div');
      probe.style.cssText = 'position:fixed;bottom:0;left:0;visibility:hidden;pointer-events:none;' +
        'height:env(safe-area-inset-bottom,0px);';
      document.body.appendChild(probe);
      out.env = parseFloat(getComputedStyle(probe).height) || 0;
      document.body.removeChild(probe);
    } catch (e) { out.env = 0; }

    out.vv_vs_inner = 0;
    if (window.visualViewport) {
      out.vv_vs_inner = Math.max(0, window.innerHeight - window.visualViewport.height);
    }
    out.vv_vs_layout = 0;
    if (window.visualViewport) {
      out.vv_vs_layout = Math.max(0, document.documentElement.clientHeight - window.visualViewport.height);
    }
    out.avail_vs_inner = 0;
    if (window.screen && window.screen.availHeight) {
      out.avail_vs_inner = Math.max(0, window.screen.availHeight - window.innerHeight);
    }
    var appHpx = parseFloat(getComputedStyle(document.documentElement).getPropertyValue('--app-height')) || 0;
    out.apph_vs_inner = appHpx > 0 ? Math.max(0, window.innerHeight - appHpx) : 0;
    return out;
  }

  var _safeAreaPanel = null;
  function _renderSafeAreaPanel(sig) {
    if (!SHOW_SAFE_AREA_PANEL) return;
    if (!_safeAreaPanel) {
      _safeAreaPanel = document.createElement('div');
      _safeAreaPanel.style.cssText = 'position:fixed;top:4px;left:4px;z-index:999999;' +
        'background:rgba(0,0,0,0.75);color:#0f0;font:10px monospace;' +
        'padding:4px 6px;border-radius:4px;pointer-events:none;white-space:pre;';
      document.body.appendChild(_safeAreaPanel);
    }
    // Raw numbers only, side by side — no "best" pick shown here anymore.
    // Godot's own admin log (GODOT_SAFE_AREA ... -> chosen=...) is the
    // place that shows which one actually got used, so the two logs
    // together tell the full story: what JS measured vs what Godot chose.
    _safeAreaPanel.textContent =
      'env=' + sig.env.toFixed(0) +
      ' vvIn=' + sig.vv_vs_inner.toFixed(0) +
      ' vvLay=' + sig.vv_vs_layout.toFixed(0) +
      ' avail=' + sig.avail_vs_inner.toFixed(0) +
      ' appH=' + sig.apph_vs_inner.toFixed(0);
  }

  function _reportSafeArea(tag) {
    var sig = _measureSafeAreaSignals();
    _renderSafeAreaPanel(sig);
    var msg = 'SAFE_AREA_REPORT[' + tag + '] env=' + sig.env.toFixed(1) +
      ' vv_vs_inner=' + sig.vv_vs_inner.toFixed(1) +
      ' vv_vs_layout=' + sig.vv_vs_layout.toFixed(1) +
      ' avail_vs_inner=' + sig.avail_vs_inner.toFixed(1) +
      ' apph_vs_inner=' + sig.apph_vs_inner.toFixed(1);
    if (DEV) window._earlyLog(msg, '#0ff');
    if (window._enqueueLog) window._enqueueLog('info', msg);
    window._lastSafeAreaSignals = sig; // Godot reads the raw numbers from here
    return sig;
  }

  _reportSafeArea('initial');
  setTimeout(function(){ _reportSafeArea('t+300ms'); }, 300);
  setTimeout(function(){ _reportSafeArea('t+1000ms'); }, 1000);
  window.addEventListener('resize', function(){ _reportSafeArea('resize'); });
  if (window.visualViewport) {
    window.visualViewport.addEventListener('resize', function(){ _reportSafeArea('vv-resize'); });
  }

  var missing=Engine.getMissingFeatures({threads:false});
  if(DEV) window._earlyLog('missing: ['+missing.join(',')+']');
  if (missing.length > 0) {
    // Previously only logged in DEV — in prod this fell through to
    // startGame() anyway, which either eventually rejects deep in WASM
    // setup (no friendly message, since that path only calls
    // displayFailureNotice from the .then() rejection handler below) or, on
    // some devices/browsers, just hangs the loading screen forever with no
    // visible error and no log sent at all if the failure is a synchronous
    // throw during Engine setup that never reaches that rejection handler.
    // Best we can do: fail fast with a clear message instead of a silent
    // stuck spinner, and report it as an error immediately (not debounced,
    // see _enqueue's per-level delay) so the admin Logs tab actually shows
    // how many real users are hitting this and on what device/browser —
    // _probeCapabilities() above already sent the raw webgl1/webgl2/gpu
    // facts for this exact session right before this, so the two log lines
    // pair up by device/ip/time in the admin panel.
    var missMsg = 'Unsupported device/browser — missing: ' + missing.join(', ') +
      ' (webgl1=' + _caps.webgl1 + ' webgl2=' + _caps.webgl2 + ')';
    console.error(missMsg);
    statusNotice.innerHTML = 'Your device or browser doesn\'t support what this game needs to run ('
      + missing.join(', ') + '). Try updating your browser/app, or use a different device.';
    setStatusMode('notice');
    return;
  }

  setStatusMode('progress');
  var _last=-1;
  var _gameStarted=false;
  var _loadStage = 'downloading';       // downloading -> download-complete -> (engine resolves or hangs after this)
  var _lastProgressAt = Date.now();     // updated every time the % actually changes
  var _loadStartAt = Date.now();

  // Best-effort snapshot of the wasm/pck network requests via the Resource
  // Timing API — lets a stall report distinguish "still actively
  // downloading, just slow" from "download already finished ages ago, hung
  // afterward in WASM compile/instantiate/thread-init" (which is the classic
  // symptom of a cross-origin-isolation mismatch — see the COI check above).
  function _assetTimingSummary() {
    try {
      var entries = performance.getEntriesByType('resource').filter(function(e){
        return /\.(wasm|pck)(\?|$)/.test(e.name);
      });
      if (!entries.length) return 'assets=none-observed';
      return entries.map(function(e){
        var done = e.responseEnd > 0;
        var size = e.transferSize || e.encodedBodySize || 0;
        return (e.name.split('/').pop()) + ':' + (done ? 'done' : 'pending') + ':' + size + 'B';
      }).join(',');
    } catch (e) { return 'assets=probe-failed'; }
  }

  // Stall detector — on a slow/flaky connection (very plausible on mobile
  // data, which is most of this game's real traffic), the .wasm/.pck
  // download can just sit there with no progress and no error either: no
  // onProgress call, no rejection, nothing — the loading spinner spins
  // forever with zero signal that anything is wrong. That's another
  // "game just doesn't open" report we'd otherwise have no way to tell
  // apart from a genuine compatibility failure. If nothing has happened by
  // 20s, log it once (still lets it keep trying — no reload forced, in
  // case it's just a slow-but-eventually-fine load).
  //
  // Upgraded to carry enough context to actually diagnose WHICH stage it
  // died in, instead of just a frozen byte percentage: cross-origin
  // isolation state (the #1 suspect for "downloaded fine, hung after"),
  // how long since the % last actually moved (frozen-since vs slow-but-
  // moving), device/network hints, and a resource-timing snapshot of the
  // actual wasm/pck requests.
  var _stallTimer = setTimeout(function(){
    if (_gameStarted) return;
    var frozenForMs = Date.now() - _lastProgressAt;
    var conn = navigator.connection || navigator.mozConnection || navigator.webkitConnection;
    var netInfo = conn ? (conn.effectiveType + '/dl=' + conn.downlink + 'Mbps') : 'unknown';
    var stallMsg = 'LOAD_STALL: no engine start after 20s' +
      ' last_progress=' + _last + '%' +
      ' stage=' + _loadStage +
      ' frozen_for_ms=' + frozenForMs +
      ' coi=' + _coi + ' sab=' + _sab +
      ' net=' + netInfo +
      ' cores=' + (navigator.hardwareConcurrency || '?') +
      ' assets=[' + _assetTimingSummary() + ']';
    console.warn(stallMsg);
    // Explicit enqueue (not just relying on the console.warn hook) so this
    // specific diagnostic is guaranteed to reach the admin Logs tab even if
    // the generic console hook ever changes/misses a level.
    if (window._enqueueLog) window._enqueueLog('warn', stallMsg);
  }, 20000);

  engine.startGame({
    onProgress: function(cur,tot){
      if(cur>0&&tot>0){
        statusProgress.value=cur; statusProgress.max=tot;
        var pct=Math.round(cur/tot*100);
        if(pct!==_last){
          _last=pct; _lastProgressAt=Date.now();
          if (pct >= 100) _loadStage = 'download-complete';
          if(DEV&&(pct%10===0||pct===100))window._earlyLog('Loading: '+pct+'%');
        }
      } else {
        statusProgress.removeAttribute('value'); statusProgress.removeAttribute('max');
      }
    }
  }).then(function(){
    _gameStarted=true; clearTimeout(_stallTimer);
    if(DEV) window._earlyLog('✓ Game started');
    setStatusMode('hidden');
  }, function(err){
    _gameStarted=true; clearTimeout(_stallTimer); // stop the stall warning — we have a real, more specific error now
    if(DEV) window._earlyLog('❌ startGame: '+(err&&err.message?err.message:String(err)),'#f55');
    displayFailureNotice(err);
  });
}

window._startGodotSetup=initGodotGame;
if(window._godotEngineLoaded) initGodotGame();
</script>

</body>
</html>
```
